nodes.label: Scalar associativity
nodes.statement: For scalars a,b and a vector v, a(bv)=(ab)v.

nodes.label: Scalar identity
nodes.statement: For every vector v, 1v=v.

nodes.label: Distributivity over vector addition
nodes.statement: For every scalar a and vectors u,v, a(u+v)=au+av.

nodes.label: Distributivity over scalar addition
nodes.statement: For scalars a,b and a vector v, (a+b)v=av+bv.

nodes.label: Vector space / Espace vectoriel
nodes.statement: A vector space over a commutative field K is an abelian group (V,+) with scalar multiplication K×V→V satisfying scalar associativity, scalar identity and both distributive laws. Its elements are vectors.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Vector subspace / Sous-espace vectoriel
nodes.statement: A subspace U of a K-vector space V is a subset containing 0 and closed under vector addition and multiplication by every scalar in K, with the induced operations.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Linear combination and span / Combinaison linéaire et sous-espace engendré
nodes.statement: A linear combination of vectors is a finite sum ∑ a_i v_i with a_i∈K. The span of a family is the set of all its finite linear combinations, including the empty sum 0.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Linear independence / Famille libre
nodes.statement: A family (v_i) is linearly independent if every finitely supported relation ∑ a_i v_i=0 has all coefficients zero. A family failing this property is dependent.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Basis / Base
nodes.statement: A basis of V is a linearly independent family whose span is V. Coordinates relative to a basis are the coefficients in the unique finitely supported expansion of a vector.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Finite-dimensional vector space
nodes.statement: A vector space is finite-dimensional if it has a finite spanning family; otherwise it is infinite-dimensional.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dimension / Dimension
nodes.statement: The dimension of a vector space admitting a basis is the cardinality of any basis; the basis-cardinality theorem ensures independence of the choice. For a finite-dimensional space this is a natural number, with dim{0}=0.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Linear mapping / Application linéaire
nodes.statement: A map T:V→W between K-vector spaces is linear if T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v) for all a,b∈K and u,v∈V. An endomorphism is a linear map V→V.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Kernel and image of a linear mapping
nodes.statement: For a linear map T:V→W, ker T={v:T(v)=0} and im T={T(v):v∈V}. These are subspaces of V and W respectively.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Linear isomorphism / Isomorphisme linéaire
nodes.statement: A linear isomorphism is a bijective linear map. Two K-vector spaces are isomorphic if such a map exists between them. An automorphism is an isomorphism from V to itself.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Sum and internal direct sum of subspaces
nodes.statement: The sum U₁+⋯+U_r consists of sums u₁+⋯+u_r with u_i∈U_i. It is direct, written ⊕U_i, if every vector in the sum has a unique such expression. A complement of U in V is W with V=U⊕W.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Quotient vector space / Espace vectoriel quotient
nodes.statement: For a subspace U≤V, V/U is the set of additive cosets v+U with (v+U)+(w+U)=(v+w)+U and a(v+U)=av+U. The quotient map sends v to v+U.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Space of linear maps and endomorphism algebra
nodes.statement: Hom_K(V,W) is the vector space of linear maps with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. End_K(V)=Hom_K(V,V) also has composition as multiplication and identity id_V; composition is bilinear.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dual space and dual mapping / Dualité
nodes.statement: The algebraic dual V* is Hom_K(V,K). For T:V→W the dual map T*:W*→V* sends f to f∘T. Here * denotes algebraic duality; the inner-product adjoint will be denoted †.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Annihilator / Annulateur
nodes.statement: For U≤V its annihilator is U⁰={f∈V*: f(u)=0 for all u∈U}.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Subspace criterion and span
nodes.statement: A nonempty subset U of V is a subspace exactly when au+bv∈U for all u,v∈U and a,b∈K. Intersections of subspaces are subspaces. The span of S is the smallest subspace containing S.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Exchange lemma / Lemme d’échange
nodes.statement: If v₁,…,v_m are linearly independent and w₁,…,w_n span V, then m≤n and m of the w_j can be replaced by the v_i to obtain a spanning family.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Finite basis extraction and extension
nodes.statement: A finite spanning family contains a basis. In a finite-dimensional space every linearly independent family extends to a finite basis. No axiom of choice is needed for these finite assertions.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Existence and extension of arbitrary bases
nodes.statement: Assuming the axiom of choice, every linearly independent family in a vector space extends to a basis. In particular every vector space has a basis.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Invariance of basis cardinality
nodes.statement: Any two finite bases of a vector space have the same length. More generally, in ZFC any two bases have the same cardinality. The finite statement follows from exchange; choice is recorded for the general cardinal comparison.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Linear map determined by basis values
nodes.statement: For a basis (e_i) of V and an arbitrary family (w_i) in W, there is a unique linear map T:V→W with T(e_i)=w_i. It is an isomorphism exactly when (w_i) is a basis of W.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Kernel, image and injectivity
nodes.statement: The kernel and image of a linear map are subspaces. A linear map is injective exactly when its kernel is {0}.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: First isomorphism theorem for vector spaces
nodes.statement: For a linear map T:V→W, v+ker T↦T(v) is a well-defined linear isomorphism V/ker T→im T.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Rank–nullity theorem / Théorème du rang
nodes.statement: For linear T:V→W with V finite-dimensional, dim V=dim ker T+dim im T. Rank is dim im T and nullity is dim ker T.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dimension of sums and quotients
nodes.statement: For subspaces U,W of finite-dimensional V, dim(U+W)=dim U+dim W−dim(U∩W) and dim(V/U)=dim V−dim U. Every subspace of finite-dimensional V has a complement.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Classification by finite dimension
nodes.statement: Every n-dimensional K-vector space is isomorphic to Kⁿ. Two finite-dimensional K-vector spaces are isomorphic exactly when their dimensions agree. For an endomorphism in finite dimension, injectivity, surjectivity and invertibility are equivalent.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dual basis and finite-dimensional biduality
nodes.statement: If e₁,…,e_n is a basis of V, the coordinate functionals e¹,…,eⁿ form a basis of V*. Thus dim V*=dim V, and evaluation v↦(f↦f(v)) is an isomorphism V→V**.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Annihilator dimension and dual rank
nodes.statement: In finite dimension, dim U⁰=dim V−dim U. For T:V→W, ker T*=(im T)⁰ and rank T*=rank T.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Matrix / Matrice
nodes.statement: An m×n matrix over K is an array (a_ij) with entries in K. It defines a linear map Kⁿ→Kᵐ by (Ax)_i=∑_j a_ij x_j. Addition and scalar multiplication are entrywise.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Matrix product and inverse
nodes.statement: For A∈Kᵐˣⁿ and B∈Kⁿˣᵖ, (AB)_ij=∑_k a_ik b_kj. The identity I_n has diagonal entries 1 and other entries 0. A square matrix is invertible if AB=BA=I_n for some B, denoted A⁻¹.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Matrix of a linear map and change of basis
nodes.statement: Given ordered bases E=(e_j) of V and F=(f_i) of W, [T]_{F←E} has j-th column the F-coordinates of T(e_j). A change-of-basis matrix converts coordinates between two ordered bases of the same space.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Matrix equivalence and similarity
nodes.statement: Two m×n matrices are equivalent if B=PAQ with invertible P,Q of the appropriate sizes. Two square matrices are similar if B=P⁻¹AP for some invertible P. Similarity represents a change of basis of one endomorphism.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Matrix rank and linear system
nodes.statement: The rank of A is the dimension of the image of x↦Ax. Its column space is the span of its columns; its row space is the span of its rows. A linear system is an equation Ax=b; the homogeneous system has b=0.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Row operations and reduced row echelon form
nodes.statement: Elementary row operations interchange two rows, multiply one row by a nonzero scalar, or add a scalar multiple of one row to another. In reduced row echelon form, zero rows are last; each nonzero row has leading entry 1 strictly to the right of the preceding pivot, and a pivot is the only nonzero entry in its column.

bibliography.locator: II, §7, no. 6; II, §10, nos. 12–13 (linear systems and matrix reduction)

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Transpose and conjugate transpose
nodes.statement: The transpose satisfies (Aᵀ)_ij=a_ji. For a complex matrix its conjugate transpose is A†=conj(A)ᵀ; for real matrices A†=Aᵀ.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Trace / Trace
nodes.statement: For a square matrix A, tr A=∑_i a_ii. For an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space its trace is the trace of its matrix in any basis; similarity invariance ensures this is well-defined.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Multilinear and alternating forms
nodes.statement: A map f:Vʳ→K is multilinear if it is linear in each argument separately. It is alternating if it vanishes whenever two arguments are equal. This vanishing definition applies also in characteristic 2.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Determinant / Déterminant
nodes.statement: For n≥1 the determinant det:Kⁿˣⁿ→K is the unique function multilinear and alternating in the columns with det I_n=1. Set det of the empty 0×0 matrix to 1. For an endomorphism, det T is the determinant of any representing matrix.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Minor, cofactor and adjugate
nodes.statement: A minor is the determinant of a square submatrix. The cofactor C_ij of a square matrix A is (−1)^(i+j) times the minor deleting row i and column j. Its adjugate has entries adj(A)_ij=C_ji.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Matrix representation and composition
nodes.statement: For finite-dimensional V,W, T↦[T]_{F←E} is a vector-space isomorphism Hom_K(V,W)→Kᵐˣⁿ. With compatible bases [S∘T]=[S][T]. A square matrix is invertible exactly when its associated linear map is bijective.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Change-of-basis formula
nodes.statement: If P converts new domain coordinates to old and Q converts new codomain coordinates to old, then A_new=Q⁻¹A_old P. For an endomorphism using the same basis on both sides this gives A_new=P⁻¹A_old P.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Row rank equals column rank
nodes.statement: For a finite matrix, the dimension of its row space equals the dimension of its column space and equals its rank. Equivalent matrices have the same rank and every rank-r matrix is equivalent to a rectangular block matrix with I_r and zeros.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Gaussian elimination and solution spaces
nodes.statement: Elementary row operations preserve the solutions of an augmented system. Every matrix has a unique reduced row echelon form. Ax=b is consistent exactly when rank A=rank[A|b]. If x₀ is a solution, all solutions are x₀+ker A; a consistent system with n unknowns and rank r has n−r free parameters.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Trace identities
nodes.statement: For compatible rectangular matrices tr(AB)=tr(BA). Consequently trace is invariant under similarity. It is linear, and the trace of a triangular matrix is the sum of its diagonal entries.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Existence and uniqueness of determinant
nodes.statement: There is a unique normalized alternating multilinear function of n columns in Kⁿ. It is given by det A=∑_{σ∈S_n}sgn(σ)∏_{i=1}^n a_{i,σ(i)}, where S_n is the set of permutations and sgn(σ)=(−1) to the number of inversions.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Determinant product, transpose and triangular formulas
nodes.statement: For square matrices of equal size, det(AB)=det A det B and det(Aᵀ)=det A. The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its diagonal entries. Hence determinant is invariant under similarity.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Laplace expansion and adjugate identity
nodes.statement: Expansion along row i gives det A=∑_j a_ij C_ij, with the analogous column formula. Moreover A adj(A)=adj(A)A=(det A)I.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Invertibility criterion and Cramer rule
nodes.statement: A square matrix A over K is invertible exactly when det A≠0; then A⁻¹=adj(A)/det A. If Ax=b and det A≠0, x_i=det A_i/det A, where A_i replaces column i of A by b.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Invariant subspace, eigenvalue and eigenspace
nodes.statement: U≤V is invariant under T∈End_K(V) if T(U)⊆U. A scalar λ is an eigenvalue if Tv=λv for some v≠0. Its eigenspace is E_λ=ker(T−λI).

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Operator polynomial and minimal polynomial
nodes.statement: A polynomial p(t)=∑_{j=0}^r a_j t^j acts on T by p(T)=∑ a_j T^j with T⁰=I. In finite dimension the minimal polynomial m_T is the monic polynomial of least degree with m_T(T)=0. For the zero-dimensional space m_T=1.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Characteristic polynomial and multiplicities
nodes.statement: For an endomorphism of dimension n, χ_T(t)=det(tI−[T]) is its characteristic polynomial, independent of basis. The algebraic multiplicity of λ is its root multiplicity in χ_T; its geometric multiplicity is dim E_λ.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Diagonalisation / Diagonalisation
nodes.statement: T is diagonalizable over K if V has a basis of eigenvectors. Equivalently a representing matrix is similar over K to a diagonal matrix. Diagonalizability can change under extension of the scalar field.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Independence of distinct eigenspaces
nodes.statement: Eigenspaces for pairwise distinct eigenvalues form a direct sum. In particular, eigenvectors with distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent and an endomorphism of an n-dimensional space has at most n distinct eigenvalues.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Characteristic roots and eigenvalues
nodes.statement: For finite-dimensional V, λ∈K is an eigenvalue exactly when χ_T(λ)=0. Its geometric multiplicity is at most its algebraic multiplicity.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Cayley–Hamilton theorem
nodes.statement: Every endomorphism T of a finite-dimensional vector space satisfies χ_T(T)=0. In particular its minimal polynomial divides its characteristic polynomial. Polynomial divisibility here is in K[t].

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Diagonalisation criteria
nodes.statement: For an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional K-space, the following are equivalent: it is diagonalizable; V is the direct sum of its eigenspaces over K; its minimal polynomial is a product of distinct linear factors over K. Equivalently χ_T splits over K and each eigenvalue has equal algebraic and geometric multiplicities.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Distinct eigenvalues imply diagonalisation
nodes.statement: An endomorphism of an n-dimensional space with n distinct eigenvalues in K is diagonalizable over K.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Fundamental theorem of algebra — imported prerequisite
nodes.statement: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root and factors into linear factors over ℂ. This algebraic result is included as a boundary prerequisite for complex spectral theory; its proof dependencies in analysis or polynomial algebra are deferred.

bibliography.locator: Chapter 4, Factorization of Polynomials over ℂ

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Complex eigenvalue existence and triangularisation
nodes.statement: Every endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space has an eigenvalue and admits an upper-triangular matrix in some basis. More generally, over K triangularisation is possible exactly when its characteristic polynomial splits into linear factors over K.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Inner product / Produit scalaire
nodes.statement: On a real or complex vector space an inner product ⟨u,v⟩ is linear in u, satisfies ⟨u,v⟩=overline(⟨v,u⟩), and has ⟨v,v⟩>0 for v≠0. Thus it is conjugate-linear in v; over ℝ conjugation is the identity. An inner-product space is a vector space equipped with such a form.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dot product and standard Hermitian product
nodes.statement: On ℝⁿ the dot product is ⟨x,y⟩=∑ x_i y_i. On ℂⁿ the standard Hermitian product in our convention is ⟨x,y⟩=∑ x_i overline(y_i). Both are inner products.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Induced norm and distance
nodes.statement: The norm induced by an inner product is ‖v‖=√⟨v,v⟩; its distance is d(u,v)=‖u−v‖. Unit vectors have norm 1.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Orthogonality and orthogonal complement
nodes.statement: Vectors u,v are orthogonal if ⟨u,v⟩=0. For a subset S of V, S⊥={v:⟨v,s⟩=0 for all s∈S}.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Orthonormal family and orthonormal basis
nodes.statement: A family (e_i) is orthonormal if ⟨e_i,e_j⟩ equals 1 for i=j and 0 otherwise. An orthonormal basis is an orthonormal family that is an algebraic basis. Infinite Hilbert-space bases are outside this definition.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Orthogonal projection
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional subspace U of an inner-product space V, its orthogonal projection P_U maps v to the unique u∈U with v−u∈U⊥. Existence and uniqueness are supplied by orthogonal decomposition.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Adjoint of a linear map / Adjoint
nodes.statement: For T:V→W between finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, T†:W→V is the unique linear map such that ⟨Tv,w⟩=⟨v,T†w⟩ for all v,w. In orthonormal bases its matrix is the conjugate transpose of the matrix of T.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Self-adjoint, normal and positive operators
nodes.statement: An operator T on a finite-dimensional inner-product space is self-adjoint if T=T† and normal if TT†=T†T. It is positive semidefinite if it is self-adjoint and ⟨Tv,v⟩≥0 for all v; positive definite requires >0 for v≠0. Real self-adjoint matrices are symmetric; complex ones are Hermitian.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Unitary and orthogonal operators
nodes.statement: An operator U on a finite-dimensional inner-product space is unitary if U†U=UU†=I. Over ℝ it is also called orthogonal. In orthonormal coordinates a unitary matrix Q satisfies Q†Q=I; it preserves inner products.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Rayleigh quotient / Quotient de Rayleigh
nodes.statement: For self-adjoint T and v≠0, R_T(v)=⟨Tv,v⟩/⟨v,v⟩. It is real and unchanged when v is multiplied by a nonzero scalar. In standard coordinates R_A(x)=x†Ax/(x†x).

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Singular values
nodes.statement: For T:V→W between finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product spaces, its singular values are the nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of T†T, with multiplicity. This definition lists dim V values; rectangular matrix conventions often retain only min(dim V,dim W), omitting forced zeros.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Bilinear, Hermitian and quadratic forms
nodes.statement: A bilinear form b:V×V→K is linear in both arguments; it is symmetric if b(u,v)=b(v,u). Over ℂ a Hermitian form is linear in the first argument and conjugate symmetric, without positivity required. Over ℝ a quadratic form here is q(v)=b(v,v) for a symmetric bilinear b; b is recovered by polarization.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
nodes.statement: In a real or complex inner-product space, |⟨u,v⟩|≤‖u‖‖v‖. Equality holds exactly when u and v are linearly dependent, including when one vector is zero.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Norm laws and Pythagoras
nodes.statement: The induced norm satisfies positivity, ‖av‖=|a|‖v‖ and ‖u+v‖≤‖u‖+‖v‖. If u⊥v then ‖u+v‖²=‖u‖²+‖v‖². Thus the induced distance is a metric.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation
nodes.statement: Every finite linearly independent list in a real or complex inner-product space can be replaced by an orthonormal list with the same successive spans. Hence every finite-dimensional inner-product space has an orthonormal basis.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Orthogonal decomposition and projection theorem
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional subspace U of an inner-product space V, V=U⊕U⊥. If e₁,…,e_r is an orthonormal basis of U, P_U v=∑⟨v,e_i⟩e_i. It is the unique element of U minimizing ‖v−u‖.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Finite-dimensional Riesz representation
nodes.statement: For each linear functional f on a finite-dimensional inner-product space V there is a unique w∈V such that f(v)=⟨v,w⟩ for every v. The correspondence w↦f is conjugate-linear over ℂ and linear over ℝ.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Adjoint existence and identities
nodes.statement: Finite-dimensional linear maps have unique adjoints. (ST)†=T†S†, (T†)†=T and (aT+bS)†=overline(a)T†+overline(b)S†. Also ker T†=(im T)⊥ and im T†=(ker T)⊥.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Schur triangularisation
nodes.statement: Every operator on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space has an upper-triangular matrix in some orthonormal basis: A=QRQ† with Q unitary and R upper triangular.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Complex spectral theorem
nodes.statement: An operator on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space is normal if and only if it has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors. Equivalently A=QΛQ† with Q unitary and Λ diagonal. The eigenvalues of a general normal operator need not be real.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Real spectral theorem and Hermitian case
nodes.statement: Every self-adjoint operator on a finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product space has real eigenvalues and an orthonormal eigenbasis. A real symmetric matrix is QΛQᵀ with Q real orthogonal and Λ real diagonal; a Hermitian matrix is QΛQ† with Q unitary and Λ real diagonal.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Spectral decomposition by orthogonal projections
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex normal operator T, let P_λ be the orthogonal projection onto its eigenspace for each distinct eigenvalue λ. Then I=∑P_λ, P_λP_μ=0 for λ≠μ, and T=∑λP_λ. Hence p(T)=∑p(λ)P_λ for every polynomial p. The same formulas hold for real self-adjoint operators.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Rayleigh bounds and extremal eigenvalues
nodes.statement: For self-adjoint T on a nonzero finite-dimensional space, λ_min≤R_T(v)≤λ_max. Both bounds are attained; equality holds precisely for nonzero vectors in the corresponding extreme eigenspace. In an orthonormal eigenbasis the quotient is ∑λ_i|c_i|²/∑|c_i|².

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Courant–Fischer min–max theorem
nodes.statement: Let T be self-adjoint on an n-dimensional real or complex inner-product space, n≥1, with λ₁≤⋯≤λ_n repeated by multiplicity. For 1≤k≤n, λ_k=min_{dim S=k} max_{0≠v∈S} R_T(v)=max_{dim S=n−k+1} min_{0≠v∈S} R_T(v). Extrema are attained by spans of suitable eigenvectors.

bibliography.locator: Courant–Fischer theorem and proof; eigenvalue order reversed here

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Positive operators and positive square root
nodes.statement: A self-adjoint operator is positive semidefinite exactly when all its eigenvalues are ≥0, and positive definite exactly when all are >0. Every positive semidefinite operator has a unique positive semidefinite square root, obtained by replacing eigenvalues by their nonnegative square roots.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Singular value decomposition / Décomposition en valeurs singulières
nodes.statement: For every A∈ℝᵐˣⁿ or ℂᵐˣⁿ there are orthogonal or unitary matrices U,V and an m×n diagonal rectangular matrix Σ with nonnegative diagonal entries such that A=UΣV†. The number of positive singular values is rank A.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: QR factorisation
nodes.statement: If A∈ℝᵐˣⁿ or ℂᵐˣⁿ has independent columns, then A=QR where Q has n orthonormal columns and R is n×n upper triangular with positive real diagonal. With this normalization the factors are unique.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Least squares and normal equations
nodes.statement: For A∈ℝᵐˣⁿ or ℂᵐˣⁿ and b, a vector x minimizes ‖Ax−b‖ exactly when A†Ax=A†b. Minimizers exist; their images equal the orthogonal projection of b onto im A. The minimizer is unique exactly when ker A={0}, and then x=(A†A)⁻¹A†b.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Sylvester law of inertia over the reals
nodes.statement: Every real quadratic form has diagonal expression with p entries +1, q entries −1 and r zeros after an invertible change of coordinates. The triple (p,q,r) is independent of that change. It counts the positive, negative and zero eigenvalues of any symmetric representing matrix.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Polynomial over a field
nodes.statement: A polynomial over K is a formal finite sum p(t)=∑ a_j t^j, with coefficientwise addition and convolution multiplication. Its degree is the largest index of a nonzero coefficient. A root λ satisfies p(λ)=0. A polynomial splits over K if it is a nonzero constant times a product of linear factors over K.

bibliography.locator: Chapter 4; the elementary definitions extend to any field

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Generalized eigenspace and nilpotent operator
nodes.statement: For T on an n-dimensional space, n≥1, the generalized eigenspace for λ is ker(T−λI)ⁿ. An operator N is nilpotent if Nʳ=0 for some positive integer r. A Jordan block J_r(λ) has λ on its diagonal, 1 on its superdiagonal and zero elsewhere.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Polynomial division and Bézout identity
nodes.statement: For polynomials p,q over a field with q≠0, there are unique a,r with p=aq+r and r=0 or deg r<deg q. The Euclidean algorithm gives a monic greatest common divisor g and polynomials u,v with up+vq=g when p,q are not both zero. In particular coprime polynomials admit up+vq=1.

bibliography.locator: Chapter 4 (division); Bézout is the Euclidean-algorithm consequence

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Generalized eigenspace decomposition
nodes.statement: If the characteristic polynomial of T on a finite-dimensional space splits over K, V is the direct sum of its generalized eigenspaces. On the λ-summand, T is λI plus a nilpotent operator. Over ℂ the splitting hypothesis always holds.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Jordan normal form
nodes.statement: If the characteristic polynomial of T splits over K, T has a matrix which is a direct sum of Jordan blocks. The multiset of blocks is unique up to order. For each λ, the sequence dim ker(T−λI)^j determines its block sizes: the difference between consecutive nullities counts blocks of size at least j.

bibliography.locator: 8C; stated there over ℂ, with the same argument over any splitting field

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.
Selected immediate prerequisite for this formulation.

nodes.label: Zero and successor / Zéro et successeur
nodes.statement: $0\in P$ and $S\colon P\to P$ is a function. In particular, $P$ is nonempty and successor is defined everywhere on $P$.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 1; [L](#bib-l), ch. I, with the zero-based convention stated above.

bibliography.locator: ch. I, with the zero-based convention stated above.

nodes.label: Injectivity of successor
nodes.statement: For $m,n\in P$, $S(m)=S(n)$ implies $m=n$.

nodes.label: Zero is not a successor
nodes.statement: For every $n\in P$, $S(n)\ne0$.

nodes.label: Induction / Récurrence
nodes.statement: For every subset $E\subseteq P$, if $0\in E$ and $S[E]\subseteq E$, then $E=P$. Quantification over all subsets is part of this statement.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 1; [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III, for the set-theoretic formulation.

bibliography.locator: ch. III, for the set-theoretic formulation.

nodes.label: Natural numbers / Nombres naturels
nodes.statement: We take $\mathbb{N}=\omega$, the least inductive set, with $0=\varnothing$ and $S(n)=n\cup\{n\}$. Write $1=S(0)$, $2=S(1)$, and so on. This specialises the existing ST construction.

direct_dependencies.note: The natural-number set is the existing omega construction; its set-theoretic prerequisites are inherited.

nodes.label: The set-theoretic naturals satisfy the Peano axioms
nodes.statement: The set $\omega$ with $0$ and $S$ satisfies `NS-A01`–`NS-A04`. Every element is either zero or the successor of a unique natural number. Thus ZF supplies a model of this full-subset Peano presentation.
nodes.reference: [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III; [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 1 for the axiomatic comparison.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D01](#ns-d01)
proved-using [ST-T10](../cartography.md#st-t10), [ST-T11](../cartography.md#st-t11)
proved-using [ST-T10](../cartography.md#st-t10), [ST-T11](../cartography.md#st-t11)

nodes.label: Recursion on natural numbers / Définition par récurrence
nodes.statement: Given a set $X$, an element $x_0\in X$ and a function $g\colon\mathbb{N}\times X\to X$, there is a unique $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to X$ such that $f(0)=x_0$ and $f(n+1)=g(n,f(n))$. Here $n+1$ denotes $S(n)$ before addition is defined. Fixed parameters may be included in $g$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D01](#ns-d01)

nodes.label: Addition on natural numbers
nodes.statement: For each $m\in\mathbb{N}$, define $m+0=m$ and $m+S(n)=S(m+n)$. Recursion makes this a function $\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{N}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D01](#ns-d01)

nodes.label: Multiplication on natural numbers
nodes.statement: Define $m\cdot0=0$ and $m\cdot S(n)=m\cdot n+m$ for $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D02](#ns-d02)

nodes.label: Natural order / Ordre naturel
nodes.statement: For $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$, set $m\le n$ if $n=m+k$ for some $k\in\mathbb{N}$; set $m<n$ if $m\le n$ and $m\ne n$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D02](#ns-d02)

nodes.label: Natural powers / Puissances entières positives ou nulles
nodes.statement: For a natural number $a$, define $a^0=1$ and $a^{n+1}=a^n a$. The same recursion will define nonnegative integer powers in $\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$ after their multiplication is constructed. For this algebraic convention, $0^0=1$.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 1, arithmetic and recursion; [L](#bib-l), ch. V for powers in $\mathbb{C}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D03](#ns-d03)

nodes.label: Strong induction / Récurrence forte
nodes.statement: If $E\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ and, for every $n$, the condition $\{k\in\mathbb{N}:k<n\}\subseteq E$ implies $n\in E$, then $E=\mathbb{N}$. The implication at $n=0$ includes the initial case.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D04](#ns-d04)
proved-using [NS-A04](#ns-a04), [NS-T01](#ns-t01).
proved-using [NS-A04](#ns-a04), [NS-T01](#ns-t01).

nodes.label: Arithmetic laws and cancellation on natural numbers
nodes.statement: Addition and multiplication are associative and commutative; $0$ and $1$ are their respective identities, $a0=0$, and multiplication distributes over addition. Also $a+c=b+c\Rightarrow a=b$, and $ac=bc$ with $c\ne0$ implies $a=b$. A product is zero exactly when one factor is zero. For natural exponents, $a^{m+n}=a^ma^n$ and $(a^m)^n=a^{mn}$.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [NS-A02](#ns-a02), [NS-A03](#ns-a03), [NS-A04](#ns-a04), [NS-T01](#ns-t01).

proved-using [NS-A02](#ns-a02), [NS-A03](#ns-a03), [NS-A04](#ns-a04), [NS-T01](#ns-t01).

nodes.label: Discrete total order on natural numbers
nodes.statement: The relation $\le$ is a total order, with least element $0$. It agrees with $m\subseteq n$ in the von Neumann construction, while $m<n$ agrees with $m\in n$. One has $m<n\iff m+1\le n$. Addition preserves and reflects order; multiplication by a positive natural number does likewise. There is no largest natural number.

proved-using [NS-T04](#ns-t04), [NS-A04](#ns-a04), [NS-T01](#ns-t01).

proved-using [NS-T04](#ns-t04), [NS-A04](#ns-a04), [NS-T01](#ns-t01).

nodes.label: Least-element principle / Bon ordre de $\mathbb{N}$
nodes.statement: Every nonempty subset of $\mathbb{N}$ has a least element. Every nonempty subset bounded above in $\mathbb{N}$ is finite and has a greatest element.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D04](#ns-d04), [ST-D23](../cartography.md#st-d23)
uses [NS-D04](#ns-d04), [ST-D23](../cartography.md#st-d23)

proved-using [NS-T03](#ns-t03), [NS-T05](#ns-t05).

nodes.label: Integers as formal differences
nodes.statement: On $\mathbb{N}^2$, put $(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ when $a+d=b+c$. Define $\mathbb{Z}=\mathbb{N}^2/{\sim}$ and denote a class by $[a,b]$. The intended interpretation is the formal difference $a-b$, without presupposing subtraction on $\mathbb{N}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D02](#ns-d02), [ST-D09](../cartography.md#st-d09), [ST-D15](../cartography.md#st-d15)

nodes.label: Integer arithmetic and the natural embedding
nodes.statement:
Define
$$[a,b]+[c,d]=[a+c,b+d],\qquad -[a,b]=[b,a],$$
$$[a,b][c,d]=[ac+bd,ad+bc].$$
Set $0_{\mathbb Z}=[0,0]$, $1_{\mathbb Z}=[1,0]$, $x-y=x+(-y)$ and $\iota_{\mathbb N\mathbb Z}(n)=[n,0]$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D06](#ns-d06), [NS-D03](#ns-d03)
uses [NS-D06](#ns-d06), [NS-D03](#ns-d03)

nodes.label: Integer order and sign
nodes.statement: Set $[a,b]\le[c,d]$ when $a+d\le c+b$ in $\mathbb{N}$. An integer is positive, negative or nonnegative according as it is $>0$, $<0$ or $\ge0$. Strict inequality means inequality with distinct endpoints.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D04](#ns-d04), [NS-D06](#ns-d06)
uses [NS-D04](#ns-d04), [NS-D06](#ns-d06)

nodes.label: Absolute value / Valeur absolue
nodes.statement: For $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, define $|x|=x$ if $x\ge0$ and $|x|=-x$ otherwise. The same definition applies to $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ once their order and negation are defined. It gives a nonnegative number in the same system.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 5 and 7; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV for real absolute value.

bibliography.locator: ch. IV for real absolute value.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D07](#ns-d07), [NS-D08](#ns-d08)
uses [NS-D07](#ns-d07), [NS-D08](#ns-d08)

nodes.label: Well-defined construction of integers
nodes.statement: The relation in `NS-D06` is an equivalence relation. The operations in `NS-D07` do not depend on the representatives. The map $n\mapsto[n,0]$ is injective and preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$. Every integer is the image of a natural number or the negative of such an image.

uses [NS-D06](#ns-d06), [NS-D07](#ns-d07)

proved-using [NS-T04](#ns-t04), [NS-T05](#ns-t05), [ST-T08](../cartography.md#st-t08).

nodes.label: Arithmetic laws on integers
nodes.statement: Integer addition and multiplication satisfy associativity, commutativity, the identity laws and distributivity. Each $x$ has the unique additive opposite $-x$. The equation $a+x=b$ has the unique solution $x=b-a$. A product is zero exactly when a factor is zero; multiplication by a nonzero integer can be cancelled. The power identities in `NS-T04` continue to hold.

nodes.label: Ordered integer arithmetic
nodes.statement: Integer order is well-defined and total, and the natural embedding preserves and reflects it. Translation preserves and reflects order; multiplication by a positive integer preserves it, and multiplication by a negative integer reverses it. Nonempty sets of integers bounded below have a minimum; those bounded above have a maximum. For integers, $|xy|=|x||y|$ and $|x+y|\le|x|+|y|$.

nodes.label: Divisibility / Divisibilité
nodes.statement: For $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$, write $a\mid b$ if $b=ak$ for some $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. In particular $0\mid b$ holds exactly when $b=0$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D07](#ns-d07).

nodes.label: Greatest common divisor and coprimality / PGCD et nombres premiers entre eux
nodes.statement: For integers $a,b$ not both zero, $\gcd(a,b)$ is the greatest positive integer dividing both. Set $\gcd(0,0)=0$ by convention. The integers $a,b$ are coprime when $\gcd(a,b)=1$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D10](#ns-d10), [NS-D08](#ns-d08)

nodes.label: Euclidean division / Division euclidienne
nodes.statement: For $a\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, there are unique integers $q,r$ such that $a=bq+r$ and $0\le r<b$. The positive-divisor convention fixes the sign convention for the remainder.

nodes.label: Existence of the gcd and Bézout's identity
nodes.statement: For $a,b$ not both zero, their gcd $d$ exists and has a representation $d=ua+vb$ with $u,v\in\mathbb{Z}$. Every common divisor divides $d$. Consequently, if $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $a\mid bc$, then $a\mid c$.

nodes.label: Rational numbers as fractions
nodes.statement: On $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, put $(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ if $ad=bc$. Define $\mathbb{Q}$ as the quotient and write $a/b$ for the class of $(a,b)$. Positive denominators simplify the order convention; negative denominators can subsequently be rewritten by changing the sign of the numerator.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 7; [L](#bib-l), ch. II for the fraction construction.

bibliography.locator: ch. II for the fraction construction.

nodes.label: Rational arithmetic and the integer embedding
nodes.statement:
For positive $b,d$, define
$$\frac ab+\frac cd=\frac{ad+bc}{bd},\qquad \frac ab\frac cd=\frac{ac}{bd},\qquad -\frac ab=\frac{-a}{b}.$$
For $a\ne0$, define $(a/b)^{-1}=b/a$ if $a>0$ and $(-b)/(-a)$ if $a<0$. Set $x/y=xy^{-1}$ for $y\ne0$, and $\iota_{\mathbb Z\mathbb Q}(a)=a/1$. Zero and one are $0/1$ and $1/1$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D12](#ns-d12)

nodes.label: Rational order
nodes.statement: For $b,d>0$, define $a/b\le c/d$ if $ad\le bc$. Strict order and sign follow the integer conventions. Rational absolute value is defined by `NS-D09`.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D12](#ns-d12), [NS-D08](#ns-d08)
uses [NS-D12](#ns-d12), [NS-D08](#ns-d08)

nodes.label: Well-defined construction of rational numbers
nodes.statement: The fraction relation is an equivalence relation. Rational addition, multiplication, negation and nonzero reciprocal are independent of representatives. The integer embedding is injective and preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$ and negation.

nodes.label: Rational arithmetic laws and division
nodes.statement: Rational operations satisfy associativity, commutativity, identity laws and distributivity. Additive opposites are unique, and every nonzero rational has a unique multiplicative inverse. For $a\ne0$, $ax=b$ has the unique solution $x=b/a$. Nonzero factors cancel, and a product is zero exactly when a factor is zero. Natural-power identities remain valid; for $x\ne0$, set $x^{-n}=(x^{-1})^n$ to extend them to integer exponents.

nodes.label: Ordered rational arithmetic
nodes.statement: Rational order is well-defined and total. The integer embedding preserves and reflects order. Translation preserves and reflects order; positive multiplication preserves it, negative multiplication reverses it. If $0<x<y$, then $0<1/y<1/x$. Also $|xy|=|x||y|$ and $|x+y|\le|x|+|y|$.

nodes.label: Unique reduced fraction / Fraction irréductible
nodes.statement: Every rational number has a unique expression $a/b$ with $a\in\mathbb{Z}$, $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and $\gcd(a,b)=1$. For zero this expression is $0/1$.

nodes.label: Density and Archimedean property of rational numbers
nodes.statement: For $p<q$ in $\mathbb{Q}$, $p<(p+q)/2<q$. For every rational $x$, some $n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $x<n$. More generally, for $x,y>0$ rational, some $n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $nx>y$.

nodes.label: A rational gap at the square root of two
nodes.statement: There is no $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ with $q^2=2$. The set $E=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q\ge0,\ q^2<2\}$ is nonempty and bounded above in $\mathbb{Q}$, but has no supremum in $\mathbb{Q}$. Indeed a putative supremum would have square $2$: rational perturbations rule out both a smaller and a larger square. This does not yet assume the existence of $\sqrt2$ as a real number.
nodes.reference: [L](#bib-l), ch. II–III; [DD](#bib-dd), *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, rational gaps and cuts.

bibliography.locator: *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, rational gaps and cuts.

nodes.label: Upper and lower bounds / Majorant et minorant
nodes.statement: For $E\subseteq K$, an upper bound is $u\in K$ such that $x\le u$ for every $x\in E$; a lower bound is $\ell\in K$ such that $\ell\le x$ for every $x\in E$. The set is bounded above (*majoré*), bounded below (*minoré*) or bounded (*borné*) when the respective bounds exist. A bound need not belong to $E$.
nodes.reference: [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV for real bounds.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D20](../cartography.md#st-d20).

nodes.label: Minimum and maximum / Plus petit et plus grand élément
nodes.statement: A minimum of $E$ is an element of $E$ which is a lower bound of $E$; a maximum is an element of $E$ which is an upper bound. Write $\min E$ and $\max E$ when these elements exist. The empty set has neither.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D15](#ns-d15)

nodes.label: Supremum and infimum / Borne supérieure et borne inférieure
nodes.statement:
The supremum $\sup_K E$ is the least element of the set of upper bounds of $E$ in $K$. The infimum $\inf_K E$ is the greatest element of the set of lower bounds. Either may fail to exist. In French, *borne supérieure* denotes the least upper bound, while an arbitrary upper bound is a *majorant*; the corresponding lower notions are *borne inférieure* and *minorant*.

For example, $\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:0\le q,\ q^2<2\}$ has no supremum in $\mathbb{Q}$, but its embedded image will have supremum $\sqrt2$ in $\mathbb{R}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D15](#ns-d15), [NS-D16](#ns-d16)
uses [NS-D15](#ns-d15), [NS-D16](#ns-d16)

nodes.label: Archimedean property / Propriété d'Archimède
nodes.statement: For an ordered number system containing $\mathbb{N}$ and with the arithmetic laws used below, the Archimedean property says: for every $x$, there is $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $x<n$. In $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ this is equivalent to: for every $x,y>0$, some $n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $nx>y$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D04](#ns-d04)

nodes.label: Dedekind completeness / Complétude pour l'ordre
nodes.statement: A totally ordered set is Dedekind complete in the sense used here if every nonempty subset bounded above has a supremum in that set. In this convention no condition is imposed on the supremum of the empty set or of an unbounded subset. Applied to a number system with negation reversing order, this also gives infima for nonempty sets bounded below.
nodes.reference: [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III for order completeness; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV; [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 9.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D17](#ns-d17)

nodes.label: Uniqueness and attainment of bounds
nodes.statement: Suprema and infima, when they exist, are unique. If $\sup_K E\in E$, it equals $\max E$; conversely a maximum is the supremum. The dual statements hold for infimum and minimum. A nonempty finite subset of a totally ordered set has both a minimum and a maximum.

nodes.label: Dedekind cut / Coupure de Dedekind
nodes.statement: A cut is a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Q}$ which is nonempty, different from $\mathbb{Q}$, downward closed, and has no greatest element. Downward closed means that $a\in A$ and $q<a$ imply $q\in A$; having no greatest element means that for each $a\in A$ some $b\in A$ satisfies $a<b$.
nodes.reference: [L](#bib-l), ch. III; [DD](#bib-dd), *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §IV, with our one-sided convention.

bibliography.locator: *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §IV, with our one-sided convention.

nodes.label: The real-number set and its order
nodes.statement: Define $\mathbb{R}$ to be the set of all cuts, a subset of $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})$. For cuts $A,B$, put $A\le B$ if $A\subseteq B$, and $A<B$ if $A\subsetneq B$.

nodes.label: Rational embedding in the real numbers
nodes.statement: For $q\in\mathbb{Q}$, set $q^*=\{r\in\mathbb{Q}:r<q\}$ and $\iota_{\mathbb Q\mathbb R}(q)=q^*$. The cuts $0^*$ and $1^*$ will be the real zero and one.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D19](#ns-d19)

nodes.label: Addition and negation of cuts
nodes.statement:
For cuts $A,B$, define
$$A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\},$$
$$-A=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:\text{there exists }r\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus A\text{ with }q<-r\}.$$
Subtraction is $A-B=A+(-B)$. The strict inequality in the second formula deals with the possible endpoint of the complement.
nodes.reference: [L](#bib-l), ch. III–IV; [DD](#bib-dd), *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §VI, for cut arithmetic.

bibliography.locator: *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §VI, for cut arithmetic.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D19](#ns-d19), [NS-D13](#ns-d13)
uses [NS-D19](#ns-d19), [NS-D13](#ns-d13)

nodes.label: Multiplication of cuts
nodes.statement:
For $A,B\ge0^*$, set
$$AB=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q<0\}\ \cup\ \{q\in\mathbb{Q}:\exists a\in A\,\exists b\in B,\ a>0,\ b>0,\ q<ab\}.$$
For arbitrary signs, use this product of nonnegative cuts with $(-A)B=-(AB)$ when $A,B\ge0^*$ and $(-A)(-B)=AB$. Equivalently, multiply the absolute values and assign the usual sign; zero times any cut is $0^*$.

nodes.label: Reciprocal and division of real numbers
nodes.statement:
For a positive cut $A>0^*$, define
$$A^{-1}=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q\le0\}\ \cup\ \{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q>0,\ \exists r\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus A,\ r>0,\ q<1/r\}.$$
For $A<0^*$ put $A^{-1}=-((-A)^{-1})$. For $B\ne0^*$ put $A/B=AB^{-1}$. No reciprocal is assigned to zero.
nodes.reference: [L](#bib-l), ch. III–IV, real arithmetic; [DD](#bib-dd), *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §VI. The displayed formula fixes our particular one-sided encoding.

bibliography.locator: *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §VI. The displayed formula fixes our particular one-sided encoding.

nodes.label: Cuts form a totally ordered set
nodes.statement: Inclusion totally orders the cuts: for any $A,B$, either $A\subseteq B$ or $B\subseteq A$. If $A\subsetneq B$, there is a rational $q$ such that $A<q^*<B$.

nodes.label: Rational cuts preserve arithmetic and order
nodes.statement: Each $q^*$ is a cut, and $q\mapsto q^*$ is injective. It preserves and reflects order and, with the operations above, preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$, negation and nonzero reciprocal. This permits us to identify rational numbers with their images in $\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.label: Arithmetic of real cuts
nodes.statement: The formulas for addition, negation, multiplication and nonzero reciprocal yield cuts. They satisfy associativity, commutativity, identity laws and distributivity, with $0^*,1^*$ as identities. Each cut has a unique additive opposite, and each nonzero cut has a unique reciprocal. Translation preserves and reflects order, and multiplication by a positive cut preserves and reflects order. Thus the cut construction realises `NS-A05` and `NS-A06`. Absolute value satisfies $|xy|=|x||y|$ and $|x+y|\le|x|+|y|$.
nodes.reference: [L](#bib-l), ch. III–IV; [DD](#bib-dd), *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §VI; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV for the resulting real arithmetic.

nodes.label: Completeness of the real numbers / Théorème de la borne supérieure
nodes.statement:
Every nonempty subset $\mathcal E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ bounded above has a unique supremum. For the cut construction it is
$$\sup\mathcal E=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal E}A.$$
Nonemptiness ensures the union is nonempty, and an upper cut bounds the union away from all of $\mathbb{Q}$. Downward closure and absence of a greatest element pass to the union. It is the least upper bound for inclusion.
nodes.reference: [L](#bib-l), ch. IV; [DD](#bib-dd), *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, §V; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV for completeness.

nodes.label: Arithmetic axioms for a real-number presentation
nodes.statement: The operations $+,\cdot\colon K^2\to K$ are associative and commutative; $0\ne1$; $x+0=x$ and $x1=x$; multiplication distributes over addition. Every $x$ has an additive opposite, and every $x\ne0$ has a multiplicative inverse.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 7 and 9; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV for the real-number instance.

bibliography.locator: ch. IV for the real-number instance.

nodes.label: Order compatible with arithmetic
nodes.statement: The relation $\le$ is a total order on $K$. If $x\le y$, then $x+z\le y+z$ for every $z$. If $0\le x$ and $0\le y$, then $0\le xy$. Together with `NS-A05`, these conditions imply $0<1$ and strict positivity of products of positive elements.

nodes.label: Least-upper-bound axiom / Axiome de la borne supérieure
nodes.statement: Every nonempty subset $E\subseteq K$ bounded above in $K$ has a supremum in $K$. The quantifier ranges over all subsets. With `NS-A05` and `NS-A06`, this characterises the real-number system up to the unique order- and arithmetic-preserving identification fixing $1$.

nodes.label: Infima and order duality
nodes.statement:
Every nonempty real subset $E$ bounded below has an infimum, and
$$\inf E=-\sup(-E),\qquad -E=\{-x:x\in E\}.$$
The corresponding supremum identity holds when $E$ is nonempty and bounded above. Within $\mathbb{R}$, the empty set has neither a supremum nor an infimum; an unbounded-above set has no real supremum. Symbols $\pm\infty$ are not real numbers and are not adjoined here.

nodes.label: Approximation characterisation of supremum and infimum
nodes.statement: For nonempty $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ and $s\in\mathbb{R}$, $s=\sup E$ exactly when $s$ is an upper bound and, for every $\varepsilon>0$, some $x\in E$ satisfies $s-\varepsilon<x\le s$. Dually, $t=\inf E$ exactly when $t$ is a lower bound and, for every $\varepsilon>0$, some $x\in E$ satisfies $t\le x<t+\varepsilon$. These are order statements; no convergence notion is needed.

nodes.label: Arithmetic of suprema and infima
nodes.statement: If $E,F\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ are nonempty and bounded above, then $\sup(E+F)=\sup E+\sup F$, where $E+F=\{x+y:x\in E,y\in F\}$. For $c>0$, $\sup(cE)=c\sup E$. For $c<0$ and nonempty $E$ bounded below, $\sup(cE)=c\inf E$. If $\varnothing\ne E\subseteq F$ and $F$ is bounded above, then $\sup E\le\sup F$. Dual statements follow by negation. If $E$ is nonempty, then $0E=\{0\}$.
nodes.reference: [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV, ordered real arithmetic; [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III for monotonicity of bounds.

bibliography.locator: ch. III for monotonicity of bounds.

nodes.label: Archimedean property of real numbers
nodes.statement: For every real $x$ there is $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $x<n$. Consequently, for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is $n\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ such that $0<1/n<\varepsilon$. One proof supposes $\mathbb{N}$ bounded, takes its supremum $s$, and uses an integer larger than $s-1$ to contradict the upper-bound property of $s$.

nodes.label: Irrational number / Nombre irrationnel
nodes.statement: A real number is irrational if it does not belong to the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ under the rational embedding. Thus the irrational numbers form $\mathbb{R}\setminus\iota_{\mathbb Q\mathbb R}[\mathbb{Q}]$. For example, the positive square root of $2$ is irrational once its existence is established.

uses [NS-D20](#ns-d20), [NS-D21](#ns-d21)

nodes.label: Real intervals / Intervalles réels
nodes.statement: For $a<b$ in $\mathbb{R}$, define $(a,b)=\{x:a<x<b\}$, $[a,b]=\{x:a\le x\le b\}$ and the two half-open variants by mixing these inequalities. Define rays such as $(a,+\infty)=\{x:x>a\}$; here $+\infty$ is an endpoint notation. The interval $[a,a]$ is $\{a\}$, and $(a,a)$ is empty.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D20](#ns-d20)

nodes.label: Floor and ceiling / Partie entière et plafond
nodes.statement: For $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $\lfloor x\rfloor$ is the integer $m$ such that $m\le x<m+1$; $\lceil x\rceil$ is the integer $n$ such that $n-1<x\le n$. Existence and uniqueness are part of `NS-T27`.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D08](#ns-d08), [NS-D20](#ns-d20)
uses [NS-D08](#ns-d08), [NS-D20](#ns-d20)

nodes.label: Existence of integer parts
nodes.statement: Every real number has a unique floor and ceiling. They satisfy $\lceil x\rceil=-\lfloor-x\rfloor$ and, for $k\in\mathbb{Z}$, $\lfloor x+k\rfloor=\lfloor x\rfloor+k$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D27](#ns-d27)
proved-using [NS-T09](#ns-t09), [NS-T20](#ns-t20), [NS-T26](#ns-t26).
proved-using [NS-T09](#ns-t09), [NS-T20](#ns-t20), [NS-T26](#ns-t26).
proved-using [NS-T09](#ns-t09), [NS-T20](#ns-t20), [NS-T26](#ns-t26).

nodes.label: Rational and irrational numbers between real numbers
nodes.statement: For any real $x<y$, there are $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ and $r\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ with $x<q<y$ and $x<r<y$, using the canonical identification of $\mathbb{Q}$. In particular, for $a<b$, $\inf(a,b)=a$ and $\sup(a,b)=b$, although neither endpoint belongs to the interval.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [NS-T26](#ns-t26), [NS-T27](#ns-t27), [NS-T17](#ns-t17), [NS-T29](#ns-t29).
proved-using [NS-T26](#ns-t26), [NS-T27](#ns-t27), [NS-T17](#ns-t17), [NS-T29](#ns-t29).
proved-using [NS-T26](#ns-t26), [NS-T27](#ns-t27), [NS-T17](#ns-t17), [NS-T29](#ns-t29).
proved-using [NS-T26](#ns-t26), [NS-T27](#ns-t27), [NS-T17](#ns-t17), [NS-T29](#ns-t29).

nodes.label: Real roots / Racines réelles
nodes.statement: For $a\ge0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}$, $\sqrt[n]{a}$ denotes the unique nonnegative real $b$ satisfying $b^n=a$. When $n$ is odd this notation extends to negative $a$ by $\sqrt[n]{a}=-\sqrt[n]{-a}$. The existence assertion is supplied by the next theorem. For $n=2$ write $\sqrt a$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D05](#ns-d05), [NS-D20](#ns-d20)
uses [NS-D05](#ns-d05), [NS-D20](#ns-d20)

nodes.label: Existence and uniqueness of positive roots
nodes.statement: For $a\ge0$ and positive integer $n$, there is exactly one $b\ge0$ with $b^n=a$. For $a>0$ it is positive. Odd powers give a unique real root for every real $a$; an even power of a real number cannot be negative. A proof for $a>0$ takes the supremum of $\{x\ge0:x^n\le a\}$ and uses finite binomial estimates to exclude $b^n<a$ and $b^n>a$. No continuity theorem is required for this proof.
nodes.reference: [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV; [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 11, for roots. The indicated proof is the elementary supremum route.

bibliography.locator: ch. 11, for roots. The indicated proof is the elementary supremum route.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D28](#ns-d28), [NS-D05](#ns-d05)
uses [NS-D28](#ns-d28), [NS-D05](#ns-d05)
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T24](#ns-t24).
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T24](#ns-t24).
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T24](#ns-t24).

nodes.label: Uniqueness of the complete ordered number system
nodes.statement: If $K$ satisfies `NS-A05`–`NS-A07`, there exists a unique bijection $f\colon\mathbb{R}\to K$ preserving $0,1$, addition, multiplication and order. Here the rational copy in $K$ is generated by $1$, additive opposites and nonzero inverses. The map can be constructed by sending a cut $A$ to the supremum in $K$ of its rational image. This supplies the precise sense in which the real construction is independent of its coding.
nodes.reference: [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV; [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 9–11 for completeness and comparison of real-number presentations.

bibliography.locator: ch. 9–11 for completeness and comparison of real-number presentations.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T26](#ns-t26) and the rational-density argument of [NS-T28](#ns-t28), applied in both systems.
proved-using [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T26](#ns-t26) and the rational-density argument of [NS-T28](#ns-t28), applied in both systems.

nodes.label: Complex numbers as ordered pairs
nodes.statement: Define $\mathbb{C}=\mathbb{R}^2$. Equality is componentwise. After the operations below are introduced, write $(a,b)=a+ib$, where $i=(0,1)$. Define $\operatorname{Re}(a,b)=a$ and $\operatorname{Im}(a,b)=b$; the imaginary part is a real number.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D20](#ns-d20), [ST-D09](../cartography.md#st-d09)
uses [NS-D20](#ns-d20), [ST-D09](../cartography.md#st-d09)

nodes.label: Complex arithmetic
nodes.statement:
Define
$$(a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d),\qquad -(a,b)=(-a,-b),$$
$$(a,b)(c,d)=(ac-bd,ad+bc).$$
The zero and one are $(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$. For $(a,b)\ne(0,0)$ define
$$(a,b)^{-1}=\left(\frac a{a^2+b^2},\frac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\right).$$
Division by a nonzero complex number is multiplication by its reciprocal.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D29](#ns-d29), [NS-D24](#ns-d24)
uses [NS-D29](#ns-d29), [NS-D24](#ns-d24)

nodes.label: Real embedding and imaginary unit
nodes.statement: Set $\iota_{\mathbb R\mathbb C}(a)=(a,0)$ and $i=(0,1)$. Under the real embedding every complex number has the form $a+ib$. A purely imaginary number has real part zero; with this convention zero is both real and purely imaginary.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D29](#ns-d29), [NS-D30](#ns-d30)
uses [NS-D29](#ns-d29), [NS-D30](#ns-d30)

nodes.label: Complex conjugation / Conjugaison
nodes.statement: For $z=a+ib$, define $\overline z=a-ib$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D29](#ns-d29), [NS-D31](#ns-d31).
uses [NS-D29](#ns-d29), [NS-D31](#ns-d31).

nodes.label: Complex modulus / Module
nodes.statement: For $z=a+ib$, define $|z|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$. For an embedded real number this agrees with its real absolute value.

nodes.label: Complex arithmetic and unique real coordinates
nodes.statement: Complex addition and multiplication satisfy associativity, commutativity, identity laws and distributivity. The real embedding is injective and preserves arithmetic. Every $z\in\mathbb{C}$ has a unique expression $a+ib$ with $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, and $i^2=-1$. Nonnegative integer powers are defined by the same recursion as before.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [ST-T05](../cartography.md#st-t05).
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [ST-T05](../cartography.md#st-t05).

nodes.label: Complex reciprocal and cancellation
nodes.statement: For $z=a+ib\ne0$, $a^2+b^2>0$, so the reciprocal formula is defined and gives the unique $w$ with $zw=1$. Consequently, nonzero factors cancel, a product vanishes exactly when one factor vanishes, and $az=b$ with $a\ne0$ has the unique solution $z=b/a$. Integer powers of nonzero complex numbers are defined using reciprocals.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D30](#ns-d30)
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T31](#ns-t31).
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T31](#ns-t31).

nodes.label: Conjugation identities
nodes.statement:
For $z,w\in\mathbb{C}$,
$$\overline{z+w}=\overline z+\overline w,\quad \overline{zw}=\overline z\,\overline w,\quad \overline{\overline z}=z.$$
Moreover $z=\overline z$ exactly when $z$ is real, and $z\overline z=(\operatorname{Re}z)^2+(\operatorname{Im}z)^2$. If $z\ne0$, then $z^{-1}=\overline z/|z|^2$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D32](#ns-d32), [NS-D33](#ns-d33)
uses [NS-D32](#ns-d32), [NS-D33](#ns-d33)
proved-using [NS-T31](#ns-t31), [NS-T32](#ns-t32).
proved-using [NS-T31](#ns-t31), [NS-T32](#ns-t32).

nodes.label: Modulus identities and triangle inequality
nodes.statement:
For $z,w\in\mathbb{C}$, $|z|\ge0$, with equality exactly when $z=0$; $|\overline z|=|z|$; $|zw|=|z||w|$; and
$$|z+w|\le|z|+|w|,\qquad \bigl||z|-|w|\bigr|\le|z-w|.$$
For $w\ne0$, $|z/w|=|z|/|w|$. Also $|\operatorname{Re}z|,|\operatorname{Im}z|\le|z|$. These follow from real inequalities and conjugation; a general normed-space theory is not needed here.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D33](#ns-d33)
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T29](#ns-t29), [NS-T33](#ns-t33).
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T29](#ns-t29), [NS-T33](#ns-t33).
proved-using [NS-T21](#ns-t21), [NS-T29](#ns-t29), [NS-T33](#ns-t33).

nodes.label: No total order compatible with complex arithmetic
nodes.statement: There is no total order on $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying the compatibility conditions of `NS-A06` with its usual arithmetic. In any such order every nonzero square would be positive, while $i^2=-1$ and $1>0$. This does not forbid putting unrelated total orders on the underlying set; it excludes an order compatible with these operations. Supremum and infimum in this chapter therefore apply to real coordinates or moduli, with their real order, rather than to complex numbers as an ordered arithmetic system.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-A06](#ns-a06)
proved-using [NS-T31](#ns-t31).

nodes.label: Complex square roots and quadratic equations
nodes.statement: Every complex number has a square root; a nonzero complex number has exactly two, opposite to each other. This follows by solving $(u+iv)^2=a+ib$ using $r=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, $u^2=(r+a)/2$, $v^2=(r-a)/2$ and a sign choice enforcing $2uv=b$. Consequently, if $a\ne0$, the solutions of $az^2+bz+c=0$ are $(-b\pm w)/(2a)$, where $w^2=b^2-4ac$; the two solutions coincide exactly when the discriminant is zero. General polynomial root existence is deferred to algebra.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), [appendix B](https://public.csusm.edu/aitken_html/m378_summer2019/AppendixComplexNumbers.pdf), for the broader root-existence result by polar coordinates; the displayed square-root argument uses only the arithmetic of ch. 12 and real roots. [L](#bib-l), ch. V, supplies the underlying complex arithmetic.

bibliography.locator: [appendix B](https://public.csusm.edu/aitken_html/m378_summer2019/AppendixComplexNumbers.pdf), for the broader root-existence result by polar coordinates; the displayed square-root argument uses only the arithmetic of ch. 12 and real roots.
ch. V, supplies the underlying complex arithmetic.

uses [NS-D30](#ns-d30), [NS-D33](#ns-d33)
proved-using [NS-T29](#ns-t29), [NS-T31](#ns-t31), [NS-T32](#ns-t32).
proved-using [NS-T29](#ns-t29), [NS-T31](#ns-t31), [NS-T32](#ns-t32).
proved-using [NS-T29](#ns-t29), [NS-T31](#ns-t31), [NS-T32](#ns-t32).

nodes.label: Canonical embeddings / Plongements canoniques
nodes.statement:
The chosen maps are
$$n\longmapsto[n,0],\qquad a\longmapsto a/1,\qquad q\longmapsto q^*,\qquad x\longmapsto(x,0).$$
Their composites identify each earlier number system with its image in the later ones. The conventional notation $\mathbb{N}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\subseteq\mathbb{Q}\subseteq\mathbb{R}\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ always uses these identifications; the raw set encodings need not be literal nested subsets.
nodes.reference: [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 4, 7 and 12; [L](#bib-l), ch. III–V for incorporation of earlier systems.

bibliography.locator: ch. III–V for incorporation of earlier systems.

nodes.label: Compatibility of the tower of number systems
nodes.statement: Each canonical map is injective and preserves $0,1$, addition and multiplication. It preserves negation and reciprocals wherever these operations exist in the source. Through $\mathbb{R}$ it also preserves and reflects order. The extensions are proper: $-1$ is not natural, $1/2$ is not integral, $\sqrt2$ is not rational, and $i$ is not real. All earlier arithmetic equalities therefore remain valid after these identifications.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [NS-D34](#ns-d34)

nodes.label: Cardinalities of the number systems
nodes.statement: The sets $\mathbb{N},\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Q}$ are countably infinite. The sets $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$ have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ and are uncountable. The same holds for the irrational reals. For the cut construction, the upper bound comes from $\mathbb{R}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})$; a lower bound is obtained by assigning to each binary sequence the cut determined by its finite base-three partial sums with digits $0$ and $2$. This can be formulated with rational inequalities and the supremum property, without introducing an infinite-series chapter.
nodes.reference: [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III, cardinal comparison; [BT](#bib-bt), ch. IV, real numbers; [AH](#bib-ah), ch. 11.

proved-using [ST-T14](../cartography.md#st-t14), [ST-T17](../cartography.md#st-t17), [ST-T31](../cartography.md#st-t31), [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T37](#ns-t37).
proved-using [ST-T14](../cartography.md#st-t14), [ST-T17](../cartography.md#st-t17), [ST-T31](../cartography.md#st-t31), [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T37](#ns-t37).
