proved-using [ST-T14](../cartography.md#st-t14), [ST-T17](../cartography.md#st-t17), [ST-T31](../cartography.md#st-t31), [NS-T22](#ns-t22), [NS-T37](#ns-t37).

nodes.label: Uniqueness of a full-subset Peano system
nodes.statement: If $(P,0_P,S_P)$ satisfies `NS-A01`–`NS-A04`, there is a unique bijection $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to P$ such that $f(0)=0_P$ and $f(n+1)=S_P(f(n))$. Once addition and multiplication on $P$ are recursively defined, this bijection preserves them as well. Recursion constructs $f$, the successor axioms give injectivity, and full-subset induction on $P$ gives surjectivity. The last step is why the stated induction convention matters.
nodes.reference: [DD](#bib-dd), *The Nature and Meaning of Numbers*, for simply infinite systems and their identification; [BS](#bib-bs), ch. III for natural-number recursion.

bibliography.locator: *The Nature and Meaning of Numbers*, for simply infinite systems and their identification

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [NS-T02](#ns-t02), [NS-T01](#ns-t01)
proved-using [NS-T02](#ns-t02), [NS-T01](#ns-t01)

nodes.label: Set and membership / Ensemble et appartenance
nodes.statement: **Kind:** Primitive. Variables range over sets; $x\in A$ is the primitive membership relation. Equality belongs to the underlying logic. A set is not defined here as an arbitrary collection satisfying a property.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 1; [B](#bib-b), ch. I–II for the foundational language.

bibliography.locator: ch. I–II for the foundational language.

nodes.label: Formula, parameters, and axiom schema / Schéma d'axiomes
nodes.statement: **Kind:** Logical convention. A formula is a finite expression in the first-order language $\{\in,=\}$. A schema supplies one axiom for each suitable formula. Parameters are allowed and universally quantified in the resulting axiom. A schema is not quantification over all properties inside the theory.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-P01](#st-p01)

nodes.label: Extensionality / Extensionnalité
nodes.statement:
$$\forall A\,\forall B\,\bigl[\forall x\,(x\in A\leftrightarrow x\in B)\ \longrightarrow\ A=B\bigr].$$

Sets with the same members are equal.

nodes.label: Empty set / Ensemble vide
nodes.statement: $$\exists E\,\forall x\,(x\notin E).$$
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 1, for the ZF axiom system; [H](#bib-h), elementary set constructions. We display this convenient redundant axiom separately.

bibliography.locator: ch. 1, for the ZF axiom system
elementary set constructions. We display this convenient redundant axiom separately.

nodes.label: Pairing / Paire
nodes.statement: $$\forall a\,\forall b\,\exists C\,\forall x\,[x\in C\leftrightarrow(x=a\lor x=b)].$$

nodes.label: Union / Réunion
nodes.statement: $$\forall A\,\exists U\,\forall x\,[x\in U\leftrightarrow\exists B\,(B\in A\land x\in B)].$$

nodes.label: Power set / Ensemble des parties
nodes.statement:
$$\forall A\,\exists P\,\forall B\,[B\in P\leftrightarrow B\subseteq A].$$

Here $B\subseteq A$ abbreviates $\forall x\,(x\in B\to x\in A)$.

nodes.label: Separation schema / Schéma de séparation
nodes.statement:
For every formula $\varphi(x,\vec p)$ in which $B$ is not free:

$$\forall\vec p\,\forall A\,\exists B\,\forall x\,[x\in B\leftrightarrow(x\in A\land\varphi(x,\vec p))].$$

This forms a subset of a set already supplied. There is no axiom of unrestricted comprehension here.

nodes.label: Infinity / Infini
nodes.statement:
$$\exists I\,[\varnothing\in I\land\forall x\in I\,(x\cup\{x\}\in I)].$$

The empty set, pair, and union symbols abbreviate constructions from the preceding axioms.

nodes.label: Replacement schema / Schéma de remplacement
nodes.statement:
For every formula $\varphi(x,y,\vec p)$, with $B$ not free:

$$\forall\vec p\,\forall A\,\left[\bigl(\forall x\in A\,\exists!y\,\varphi(x,y,\vec p)\bigr)\to\exists B\,\forall y\,\bigl(y\in B\leftrightarrow\exists x\in A\,\varphi(x,y,\vec p)\bigr)\right].$$

A definable assignment with a unique output for each member of a set has a set of outputs. The assignment need not already be given as a set-sized function.

nodes.label: Foundation, or regularity / Fondation
nodes.statement:
$$\forall A\,[A\ne\varnothing\to\exists x\in A\,(x\cap A=\varnothing)].$$

Every nonempty set has a member disjoint from it.

nodes.label: Axiom of choice (AC) / Axiome du choix
nodes.statement: For every set $\mathcal A$ of nonempty sets, there is a function $c\colon\mathcal A\to\bigcup\mathcal A$ such that $c(A)\in A$ for each $A\in\mathcal A$.

nodes.label: Countable choice / Axiome du choix dénombrable
nodes.statement: **Status:** Additional principle over ZF, implied by AC. Every sequence $(A_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of nonempty sets admits a function $c$ with $c(n)\in A_n$.

nodes.label: Dependent choice (DC) / Axiome des choix dépendants
nodes.statement:
**Status:** Additional principle over ZF. If $X\ne\varnothing$ and $R\subseteq X\times X$ satisfies $\forall x\in X\,\exists y\in X\,xRy$, then, for each $a\in X$, there is $f\colon\omega\to X$ with $f(0)=a$ and $f(n)Rf(n+1)$ for every $n$.

Over ZF, $\mathrm{AC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The reverse implications are not theorems of ZF, assuming ZF is consistent.

nodes.label: Inclusion and proper inclusion / Inclusion
nodes.statement: $A\subseteq B$ means $\forall x\,(x\in A\to x\in B)$; $A\subsetneq B$ means $A\subseteq B$ and $A\ne B$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-P01](#st-p01).

nodes.label: Empty set / Ensemble vide
nodes.statement: $\varnothing$ denotes the unique set with no members. Existence comes from ST-A02 and uniqueness from extensionality.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-A02](#st-a02), [ST-A01](#st-a01).
uses [ST-A02](#st-a02), [ST-A01](#st-a01).

nodes.label: Singleton and unordered pair / Singleton et paire
nodes.statement: $\{a,b\}$ has exactly $a$ and $b$ as members; $\{a\}=\{a,a\}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-A03](#st-a03), [ST-A01](#st-a01).
uses [ST-A03](#st-a03), [ST-A01](#st-a01).

nodes.label: Union / Réunion
nodes.statement: $\bigcup\mathcal A=\{x:\exists A\in\mathcal A,\ x\in A\}$. Binary union is $A\cup B=\bigcup\{A,B\}$. The empty union is $\varnothing$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-A04](#st-a04), [ST-D03](#st-d03).
uses [ST-A04](#st-a04), [ST-D03](#st-d03).

nodes.label: Intersection / Intersection
nodes.statement: $A\cap B=\{x\in A:x\in B\}$. For a nonempty set $\mathcal A$ of sets, $\bigcap\mathcal A=\{x\in\bigcup\mathcal A:\forall A\in\mathcal A,\ x\in A\}$. An empty intersection is defined only relative to a specified ambient set $U$, in which case it equals $U$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-A06](#st-a06), [ST-D04](#st-d04).
uses [ST-A06](#st-a06), [ST-D04](#st-d04).

nodes.label: Difference, complement, symmetric difference / Différence
nodes.statement: $A\setminus B=\{x\in A:x\notin B\}$. The complement of $A\subseteq U$ is $U\setminus A$. Set $A\mathbin{\triangle}B=(A\setminus B)\cup(B\setminus A)$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-A06](#st-a06), [ST-D04](#st-d04).
uses [ST-A06](#st-a06), [ST-D04](#st-d04).

nodes.label: Power set / Ensemble des parties
nodes.statement: $\mathcal P(A)=\{B:B\subseteq A\}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D01](#st-d01), [ST-A05](#st-a05).
uses [ST-D01](#st-d01), [ST-A05](#st-a05).

nodes.label: Ordered pair / Couple ordonné
nodes.statement: We choose the Kuratowski encoding $(a,b)=\{\{a\},\{a,b\}\}$. Its role is to ensure $(a,b)=(c,d)$ exactly when $a=c$ and $b=d$. This encoding is a convention, not a claim about the encoding adopted by every reference.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 1; [B](#bib-b), ch. II for couples abstractly.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D03](#st-d03)

nodes.label: Cartesian product / Produit cartésien
nodes.statement: $A\times B=\{(a,b):a\in A,\ b\in B\}$. It can be obtained by separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathcal P(A\cup B))$ with the chosen pair encoding.
nodes.reference: [B](#bib-b), ch. II; [J](#bib-j), ch. 1 for the encoding.

nodes.label: Binary relation, domain, and range / Relation binaire
nodes.statement: A relation from $A$ to $B$ is a subset $R\subseteq A\times B$; $aRb$ means $(a,b)\in R$. Its domain is $\{a\in A:\exists b\in B,\ aRb\}$ and its range is $\{b\in B:\exists a\in A,\ aRb\}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D09](#st-d09), [ST-D01](#st-d01).
uses [ST-D09](#st-d09), [ST-D01](#st-d01).

nodes.label: Function or mapping / Fonction ou application
nodes.statement: A mapping $f\colon A\to B$ consists of a specified domain $A$, codomain $B$, and graph $G_f\subseteq A\times B$ with exactly one pair $(a,b)$ for each $a\in A$. We write $f(a)=b$. The codomain is recorded separately from the range and need not equal it. When treating a function as a set, we use its graph and state its domain and codomain in the surrounding notation.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D10](#st-d10).

nodes.label: Injection, surjection, and bijection / Injection, surjection, bijection
nodes.statement: $f\colon A\to B$ is injective if $f(a)=f(a')$ implies $a=a'$, surjective if every $b\in B$ is some $f(a)$, and bijective if both hold.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D11](#st-d11).

nodes.label: Composition, identity, restriction, and inverse / Composition et inverse
nodes.statement: For $f\colon A\to B$ and $g\colon B\to C$, $(g\circ f)(a)=g(f(a))$. The identity is $\mathrm{id}_A(a)=a$; $f|_S$ restricts the domain to $S\subseteq A$. A bijection has inverse $f^{-1}\colon B\to A$ determined by $f^{-1}(f(a))=a$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D11](#st-d11), [ST-D12](#st-d12).
uses [ST-D11](#st-d11), [ST-D12](#st-d12).

nodes.label: Direct image and inverse image / Image directe et image réciproque
nodes.statement: For $S\subseteq A$ and $T\subseteq B$, set $f[S]=\{f(s):s\in S\}$ and $f^{-1}[T]=\{a\in A:f(a)\in T\}$. Inverse image is defined for every mapping, including those without an inverse mapping.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D11](#st-d11), [ST-D01](#st-d01).
uses [ST-D11](#st-d11), [ST-D01](#st-d01).

nodes.label: Equivalence relation and quotient / Relation d'équivalence et quotient
nodes.statement: A relation $\sim$ on $A$ is an equivalence relation if it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Define $[a]=\{b\in A:a\sim b\}$ and $A/{\sim}=\{[a]:a\in A\}$, with quotient map $q(a)=[a]$.

nodes.label: Partition / Partition
nodes.statement: A partition of $A$ is a set of nonempty, pairwise disjoint subsets of $A$ whose union is $A$. The empty set has the empty partition.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D04](#st-d04), [ST-D05](#st-d05).
uses [ST-D04](#st-d04), [ST-D05](#st-d05).

nodes.label: Indexed family and choice function / Famille indexée
nodes.statement: A family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ is an assignment encoded by a function on the index set $I$; repetitions are allowed. A choice function on this family has domain $I$ and satisfies $c(i)\in A_i$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D11](#st-d11).

nodes.label: Indexed product and disjoint union / Produit et somme disjointe
nodes.statement: $\prod_{i\in I}A_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that $f(i)\in A_i$. The disjoint union is $\coprod_{i\in I}A_i=\{(i,a):i\in I,\ a\in A_i\}$. The empty product contains the unique empty function; the empty disjoint union is empty.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D17](#st-d17), [ST-D08](#st-d08).
uses [ST-D17](#st-d17), [ST-D08](#st-d08).

nodes.label: Function set / Ensemble d'applications
nodes.statement: $B^A=\{f:f\colon A\to B\}$, represented by graphs. It is a subset of $\mathcal P(A\times B)$. In particular, $B^{\varnothing}$ is a singleton, including when $B=\varnothing$.

nodes.label: Preorder, partial order, and linear order / Préordre et ordre
nodes.statement: A preorder is a reflexive, transitive relation $\leq$ on a set $P$. It is a partial order if also antisymmetric. A partial order is linear or total if any two elements are comparable. Its strict relation is $x<y$ when $x\leq y$ and $x\ne y$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D10](#st-d10).

nodes.label: Bounds, least and maximal elements, supremum, infimum / Bornes
nodes.statement: An upper bound of $S\subseteq P$ is $u\in P$ with $s\leq u$ for every $s\in S$. A supremum is a least upper bound. Lower bounds and infima are dual. A greatest element of $S$ belongs to $S$ and bounds it above; a maximal element of $S$ has no strictly greater member of $S$. Least and minimal elements are defined dually.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D20](#st-d20), [ST-D01](#st-d01).
uses [ST-D20](#st-d20), [ST-D01](#st-d01).

nodes.label: Chain and antichain / Chaîne et antichaîne
nodes.statement: A chain in a partially ordered set is a subset on which the induced order is linear. An antichain is a subset whose distinct elements are incomparable. The empty subset is a chain.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D20](#st-d20).

nodes.label: Well-order and order isomorphism / Bon ordre
nodes.statement: A well-order is a linear order in which every nonempty subset has a least element. An order isomorphism is a bijection preserving and reflecting the order: $x\leq y$ iff $f(x)\leq f(y)$.

nodes.label: Inductive set and successor / Ensemble inductif et successeur
nodes.statement: Set $0=\varnothing$ and $S(x)=x\cup\{x\}$. A set $I$ is inductive when $0\in I$ and $S(x)\in I$ for every $x\in I$.

nodes.label: Natural numbers / Entiers naturels
nodes.statement: $\omega$, also denoted $\mathbb N$, is the least inductive set. Its existence is established in ST-T10. We include $0$ and use the von Neumann representation $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 2; [B](#bib-b), ch. III for natural numbers.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D24](#st-d24)

nodes.label: Finite, infinite, and Dedekind-infinite sets / Ensembles finis et infinis
nodes.statement: $A$ is finite if it is bijective with some $n\in\omega$, and infinite otherwise. It is Dedekind-infinite if it is bijective with a proper subset of itself. In ZF, an infinite set need not be Dedekind-infinite; the equivalence holds in ZFC.
nodes.reference: [B](#bib-b), ch. III for the choice-based treatment; [J](#bib-j), ch. 3 and 5 for the distinction.

bibliography.locator: ch. III for the choice-based treatment

nodes.label: Countable and uncountable sets / Ensembles dénombrables
nodes.statement: We say *at most countable* if $A$ injects into $\omega$, *countably infinite* if $A$ is bijective with $\omega$, and *uncountable* if it is not at most countable. We use *countable* to include finite sets. This convention is recorded because French usage of *dénombrable* varies.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D12](#st-d12), [ST-D25](#st-d25).
uses [ST-D12](#st-d12), [ST-D25](#st-d25).

nodes.label: Transitive set / Ensemble transitif
nodes.statement: $T$ is transitive if $x\in y\in T$ implies $x\in T$, equivalently every member of $T$ is a subset of $T$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-P01](#st-p01), [ST-D01](#st-d01).
uses [ST-P01](#st-p01), [ST-D01](#st-d01).

nodes.label: Ordinal / Ordinal
nodes.statement: An ordinal is a transitive set well-ordered by membership as a strict order. Write $\alpha<\beta$ for $\alpha\in\beta$. The notation $\mathrm{Ord}$ names the class of all ordinals, which is not a set.

nodes.label: Successor and limit ordinals / Ordinaux successeurs et limites
nodes.statement: The successor of $\alpha$ is $\alpha+1=\alpha\cup\{\alpha\}$. A limit ordinal is a nonzero ordinal that is not a successor. For a set $S$ of ordinals, $\sup S=\bigcup S$; in particular $\sup\varnothing=0$.

nodes.label: Cumulative hierarchy and rank / Hiérarchie cumulative et rang
nodes.statement: By transfinite recursion, $V_0=\varnothing$, $V_{\alpha+1}=\mathcal P(V_\alpha)$, and $V_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}V_\beta$ for nonzero limit $\lambda$. The rank of $x$ is the least $\alpha$ with $x\subseteq V_\alpha$, equivalently $x\in V_{\alpha+1}$. Its existence for every set uses foundation.

nodes.label: Well-founded and extensional relations / Relations bien fondées
nodes.statement: A relation $R$ on a set $A$ is well-founded if every nonempty $B\subseteq A$ contains $b$ with no $c\in B$ satisfying $cRb$. It is extensional if distinct $x,y\in A$ have different predecessor sets $\{z\in A:zRx\}$ and $\{z\in A:zRy\}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D10](#st-d10), [ST-D01](#st-d01).
uses [ST-D10](#st-d10), [ST-D01](#st-d01).

nodes.label: Transitive closure / Clôture transitive
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{TC}(A)$ is the least transitive set containing $A$ as a subset. It can be formed as $\bigcup_{n<\omega}U_n$ with $U_0=A$ and $U_{n+1}=\bigcup U_n$.

nodes.label: Definable class and proper class / Classe et classe propre
nodes.statement: A definable class is notation $\{x:\varphi(x,\vec p)\}$ for a formula with parameters. It is proper if no set has exactly those members. In ZF, classes are a manner of speaking about formulas, not additional objects over which variables quantify. Examples include the universe $V$ and $\mathrm{Ord}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-P02](#st-p02)

nodes.label: Equipotence and comparison of sizes / Équipotence
nodes.statement: $A\simeq B$ means there is a bijection between them. Write $A\preccurlyeq B$ when there is an injection $A\to B$, and $A\prec B$ when additionally $A\not\simeq B$. These statements make sense in ZF for sets that may not be well-orderable.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D12](#st-d12).

nodes.label: Cardinal, initial ordinal, and aleph / Cardinal et aleph
nodes.statement: A cardinal is an ordinal not bijective with any smaller ordinal. For a well-orderable set $A$, $|A|$ denotes its unique equipotent cardinal. In ZFC this applies to every set. The infinite cardinals are enumerated by $\aleph_0=\omega$, $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$ the next larger cardinal, and $\aleph_\lambda=\sup_{\beta<\lambda}\aleph_\beta$ at nonzero limits. In ZF this enumerates the infinite well-orderable cardinalities.

nodes.label: Cardinal arithmetic / Arithmétique cardinale
nodes.statement: In ZFC, $\kappa+\lambda=|\kappa\amalg\lambda|$, $\kappa\lambda=|\kappa\times\lambda|$, and $\kappa^\lambda=|\{f:f\colon\lambda\to\kappa\}|$. Indexed sums and products use disjoint unions and products. In ZF the underlying set constructions remain meaningful even when the result is not well-orderable.

nodes.label: Cofinality, regular and singular cardinals / Cofinalité
nodes.statement: A subset $C\subseteq\alpha$ is cofinal if every $\beta<\alpha$ satisfies $\beta\leq\gamma$ for some $\gamma\in C$. Define $\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)$ as the least ordinal $\delta$ admitting a map $f\colon\delta\to\alpha$ with cofinal range. An infinite cardinal $\kappa$ is regular if $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)=\kappa$, singular otherwise.

nodes.label: Ordinal arithmetic / Arithmétique ordinale
nodes.statement: Define addition and multiplication recursively in the right argument: $\alpha+0=\alpha$, $\alpha+(\beta+1)=(\alpha+\beta)+1$, $\alpha\cdot0=0$, and $\alpha\cdot(\beta+1)=\alpha\cdot\beta+\alpha$. At nonzero limits take suprema. Set $\alpha^0=1$, $\alpha^{\beta+1}=\alpha^\beta\cdot\alpha$; for $\alpha>0$ take suprema at nonzero limits, while $0^\beta=0$ for $\beta>0$. Ordinal operations refer to order types; cardinal operations refer to sizes.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D30](#st-d30), [ST-T25](#st-t25).
uses [ST-D30](#st-d30), [ST-T25](#st-t25).

nodes.label: Filter and ultrafilter / Filtre et ultrafiltre
nodes.statement: A proper filter on $X$ is $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal P(X)$ with $X\in\mathcal F$, $\varnothing\notin\mathcal F$, closed under finite intersections and supersets within $X$. An ultrafilter is a proper filter maximal under inclusion. The principal ultrafilter at $x\in X$ consists of the subsets containing $x$.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 7. Bourbaki's *General Topology* will provide a further reference when topology is added.

bibliography.locator: ch. 7. Bourbaki's *General Topology* will provide a further reference when topology is added.

nodes.label: Complete lattice / Treillis complet
nodes.statement: A partially ordered set $L$ is a complete lattice if every subset has a supremum and an infimum, including the empty subset. Thus $L$ has a least and a greatest element. A map $f\colon L\to L$ is monotone if $x\leq y$ implies $f(x)\leq f(y)$.

nodes.label: Relational structure and isomorphism / Structure et isomorphisme
nodes.statement: For a fixed set $I$ of relation symbols with finite arities $n_i$, a relational structure is a set $X$ together with relations $R_i\subseteq X^{n_i}$. An isomorphism is a bijection preserving and reflecting each relation. This entry records one concrete family of structures; more general signatures can also contain functions and constants.
nodes.reference: [B](#bib-b), ch. IV, for the broader theory of structures; [J](#bib-j), ch. 12, for logical structures.

bibliography.locator: ch. IV, for the broader theory of structures

nodes.label: Model of set theory / Modèle de la théorie des ensembles
nodes.statement: A set-sized structure $(M,E)$ with nonempty domain $M$ is a model of a theory $T$ when it satisfies each sentence of $T$ in first-order semantics. The relation $E\subseteq M\times M$ need not be actual ambient membership. A transitive model is a transitive set $M$ equipped with actual membership restricted to $M$. Existence of a transitive set model of ZFC is stronger than the bare consistency assertion used in the independence statements below.

nodes.label: Constructible universe / Univers constructible
nodes.statement: For a set $X$, let $\mathrm{Def}(X)$ be the subsets of $X$ definable over $(X,\in)$ by first-order formulas with parameters from $X$. Define $L_0=\varnothing$, $L_{\alpha+1}=\mathrm{Def}(L_\alpha)$, and $L_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}L_\beta$ at nonzero limits. The class $L=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\mathrm{Ord}}L_\alpha$ is the constructible universe.

nodes.label: Equality by double inclusion
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** $A=B$ iff $A\subseteq B$ and $B\subseteq A$. In particular the empty set, unordered pairs, unions, and power sets are unique when their membership conditions are fixed.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D01](#st-d01)
proved-using [ST-A01](#st-a01).

nodes.label: Russell's argument and absence of a universal set
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** For every set $A$, the set $R=\{x\in A:x\notin x\}$ does not belong to $A$. Indeed $R\in A$ would give $R\in R\leftrightarrow R\notin R$. Consequently no set contains every set. This is a theorem excluding a universal set, not a contradiction in ZF.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-A06](#st-a06)
uses [ST-D34](#st-d34).

nodes.label: No finite membership cycles
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** There is no finite nonempty cycle $x_0\in x_1\in\cdots\in x_{n-1}\in x_0$. In particular $x\notin x$ for every set $x$. Apply foundation to the finite set of members of the proposed cycle.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-A09](#st-a09)
uses [ST-D26](#st-d26).

nodes.label: Algebra of sets and De Morgan's laws
nodes.statement:
**Background: ZF.** Union and intersection are associative, commutative, idempotent, and distribute over each other. For $A_i\subseteq U$,

$$U\setminus\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i=\bigcap_{i\in I}(U\setminus A_i),\qquad U\setminus\bigcap_{i\in I}A_i=\bigcup_{i\in I}(U\setminus A_i).$$

The intersections are relative to $U$, so the formulas include $I=\varnothing$. With complement relative to $U$, $\mathcal P(U)$ is a complete Boolean algebra; a separate algebra node will later define this structure.
nodes.reference: [B](#bib-b), ch. II; [J](#bib-j), ch. 7 for Boolean algebras.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-T01](#st-t01).

nodes.label: Ordered-pair uniqueness
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** For the Kuratowski encoding, $(a,b)=(c,d)$ iff $a=c$ and $b=d$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D08](#st-d08)
proved-using [ST-A01](#st-a01)

nodes.label: Image and inverse-image laws
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, intersections relative to the codomain, and complements. Direct image preserves arbitrary unions; $f[S\cap T]\subseteq f[S]\cap f[T]$, with equality for all $S,T\subseteq A$ iff $f$ is injective. Also $S\subseteq f^{-1}[f[S]]$ and $f[f^{-1}[U]]=U\cap f[A]$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D14](#st-d14), [ST-D12](#st-d12)
uses [ST-D14](#st-d14), [ST-D12](#st-d12)
proved-using [ST-T01](#st-t01).

nodes.label: Equivalence relations correspond to partitions
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** The equivalence classes of a relation partition its underlying set. Conversely each partition defines a unique equivalence relation by membership in the same block. These constructions are inverse to one another.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D15](#st-d15), [ST-D16](#st-d16).
uses [ST-D15](#st-d15), [ST-D16](#st-d16).

nodes.label: Universal property of the quotient
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** If $f\colon A\to B$ is constant on each class of $\sim$, there is a unique $\bar f\colon A/{\sim}\to B$ with $f=\bar f\circ q$. If $a\sim a'$ iff $f(a)=f(a')$, this gives a bijection $A/{\sim}\to f[A]$.
nodes.reference: [B](#bib-b), ch. II; ch. IV for universal mappings.

bibliography.locator: ch. II; ch. IV for universal mappings.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-T07](#st-t07).

nodes.label: Power sets as characteristic functions
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** The correspondence $S\mapsto\mathbf 1_S$ is a bijection $\mathcal P(A)\to\{0,1\}^A$, where $\mathbf 1_S(a)=1$ exactly when $a\in S$.

nodes.label: Existence of the least inductive set
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** There is a unique least inductive set $\omega$. Starting with an inductive set $I$ from infinity, separate those $x\in I$ that belong to every inductive subset of $I$. The resulting set is contained in every inductive set.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-A07](#st-a07), [ST-A05](#st-a05), [ST-A06](#st-a06)
proved-using [ST-A07](#st-a07), [ST-A05](#st-a05), [ST-A06](#st-a06)
proved-using [ST-A07](#st-a07), [ST-A05](#st-a05), [ST-A06](#st-a06)

nodes.label: Induction on the natural numbers
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** If $P\subseteq\omega$, $0\in P$, and $n\in P\Rightarrow n+1\in P$, then $P=\omega$. This also gives a formula schema with parameters by separation.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-T10](#st-t10)

nodes.label: Recursion on the natural numbers
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** Given a set $X$, $a\in X$, and $g\colon X\to X$, there is a unique $f\colon\omega\to X$ with $f(0)=a$ and $f(n+1)=g(f(n))$. A definable class assignment taking sets to sets also supports such recursion, with replacement collecting the outputs into a sequence.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D11](#st-d11)
proved-using [ST-T11](#st-t11), [ST-A08](#st-a08)
proved-using [ST-T11](#st-t11), [ST-A08](#st-a08)

nodes.label: Pigeonhole principle and uniqueness of finite size
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** For $m,n\in\omega$, an injection $m\to n$ exists iff $m\leq n$. Hence finite ordinals are bijective only when equal, and every injective self-map of a finite set is surjective.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D26](#st-d26), [ST-D12](#st-d12)
uses [ST-D26](#st-d26), [ST-D12](#st-d12)
proved-using [ST-T11](#st-t11).

nodes.label: Countability of pairs and finite sequences
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** $\omega\times\omega$ is countably infinite; for example, $(m,n)\mapsto (m+n)(m+n+1)/2+n$ is a bijection with $\omega$. The set $\omega^{<\omega}=\bigcup_{n<\omega}\omega^n$ of finite sequences is also countably infinite. Explicit encodings supply these results without countable choice.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-T12](#st-t12).

nodes.label: Dedekind infinitude and countable subsets
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** A set is Dedekind-infinite iff it contains a countably infinite subset. One direction iterates an injective nonsurjective self-map starting from a point outside its range; the other shifts a countable subset and fixes the remaining points. In ZFC every infinite set has this property.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D26](#st-d26), [ST-D27](#st-d27)
uses [ST-D26](#st-d26), [ST-D27](#st-d27)
proved-using [ST-T12](#st-t12)
the final ZFC assertion uses [ST-T18](#st-t18).

nodes.label: Countable union of countable sets
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF + countable choice; also ZFC.** If $(A_n)_{n\in\omega}$ is a family of at most countable sets, then $\bigcup_n A_n$ is at most countable. Countable choice can select an injection $A_n\to\omega$ for each $n$. If those injections are already supplied as a sequence, ZF suffices. The assertion for arbitrary families is not a theorem of ZF, assuming consistency.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D27](#st-d27), [ST-D17](#st-d17)
uses [ST-D27](#st-d27), [ST-D17](#st-d17)
proved-using [ST-A11](#st-a11), [ST-T14](#st-t14).
proved-using [ST-A11](#st-a11), [ST-T14](#st-t14).

nodes.label: Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein theorem
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** Injections $A\to B$ and $B\to A$ imply a bijection $A\to B$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D35](#st-d35), [ST-D12](#st-d12).
uses [ST-D35](#st-d35), [ST-D12](#st-d12).

nodes.label: Zermelo's well-ordering theorem
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; equivalent to AC over ZF.** Every set admits a well-order.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D23](#st-d23)

nodes.label: Zorn's lemma
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; equivalent to AC over ZF.** If a nonempty partially ordered set $P$ has an upper bound in $P$ for every chain, then $P$ has a maximal element.

nodes.label: Nonempty products of nonempty sets
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; equivalent to AC over ZF.** For every set-indexed family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ of nonempty sets, $\prod_{i\in I}A_i\ne\varnothing$. For a finite index set this follows already in ZF.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D18](#st-d18), [ST-D17](#st-d17)
uses [ST-D18](#st-d18), [ST-D17](#st-d17)

nodes.label: Sections of surjections
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; equivalent to AC over ZF.** Every surjection $f\colon A\to B$ has a right inverse $s\colon B\to A$ with $f\circ s=\mathrm{id}_B$. Choosing $s(b)$ amounts to choosing from each fibre $f^{-1}[\{b\}]$.

nodes.label: Comparability of arbitrary sizes
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; equivalent to AC over ZF.** For all sets $A,B$, either $A\preccurlyeq B$ or $B\preccurlyeq A$. The converse implication to AC follows by comparing a set with its Hartogs ordinal.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 5; [B](#bib-b), ch. III for cardinal comparison with choice.

bibliography.locator: ch. III for cardinal comparison with choice.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D35](#st-d35)

nodes.label: Ordinal representation and comparison of well-orders
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** Every well-ordered set is order-isomorphic to a unique ordinal. For any ordinals $\alpha,\beta$, exactly one of $\alpha\in\beta$, $\alpha=\beta$, and $\beta\in\alpha$ holds. Consequently two well-orders are isomorphic, or one is isomorphic to a proper initial segment of the other.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 2; [B](#bib-b), ch. III for comparison of well-orders.

bibliography.locator: ch. III for comparison of well-orders.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D23](#st-d23), [ST-D29](#st-d29)
uses [ST-D23](#st-d23), [ST-D29](#st-d29)
proved-using [ST-T29](#st-t29) as one construction of the representation.

nodes.label: Transfinite induction
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF; schema.** For a formula $\varphi$ with parameters, if for every ordinal $\alpha$ the truth of $\varphi(\beta)$ for all $\beta<\alpha$ implies $\varphi(\alpha)$, then $\varphi$ holds for every ordinal. A counterexample would yield a least counterexample by separation inside a sufficiently large ordinal.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D29](#st-d29), [ST-P02](#st-p02)
uses [ST-D29](#st-d29), [ST-P02](#st-p02)
proved-using [ST-T23](#st-t23).

nodes.label: Transfinite recursion
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF; schema.** If a definable rule $G$ assigns a unique set to each function whose domain is an ordinal, then for every ordinal $\alpha$ there is a unique function $F$ on $\alpha$ satisfying $F(\beta)=G(F|_\beta)$ for $\beta<\alpha$. These functions agree on common initial segments and describe a definable class function on $\mathrm{Ord}$.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D29](#st-d29), [ST-D13](#st-d13)
uses [ST-D29](#st-d29), [ST-D13](#st-d13)
proved-using [ST-T24](#st-t24), [ST-A08](#st-a08)
proved-using [ST-T24](#st-t24), [ST-A08](#st-a08)

nodes.label: Burali–Forti theorem
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** There is no set of all ordinals. If such a set existed, its union would be an ordinal at least as large as every ordinal, while its successor would be larger.

direct_dependencies.note: proved-using [ST-T23](#st-t23), [ST-A04](#st-a04).
proved-using [ST-T23](#st-t23), [ST-A04](#st-a04).

nodes.label: Hartogs's theorem
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** For every set $A$, there is a least ordinal $h(A)$ that does not inject into $A$. It is a cardinal. One construction collects the order types of well-orders on subsets of $A$; their collection is exactly $h(A)$. This supplies arbitrarily large well-orderable cardinals without assuming that $A$ itself is well-orderable.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D35](#st-d35), [ST-D36](#st-d36)
uses [ST-D35](#st-d35), [ST-D36](#st-d36)
proved-using [ST-T23](#st-t23), [ST-A05](#st-a05), [ST-A08](#st-a08).
proved-using [ST-T23](#st-t23), [ST-A05](#st-a05), [ST-A08](#st-a08).
proved-using [ST-T23](#st-t23), [ST-A05](#st-a05), [ST-A08](#st-a08).

nodes.label: Set induction and the rank theorem
nodes.statement:
**Background: ZF.** For every formula $\varphi$, if $\forall x\,[(\forall y\in x\,\varphi(y))\to\varphi(x)]$, then $\forall x\,\varphi(x)$. Every set belongs to some $V_\alpha$, and

$$\operatorname{rank}(x)=\sup\{\operatorname{rank}(y)+1:y\in x\}.$$

Each $V_\alpha$ is a transitive set. The union over all ordinals is the class $V$, not a set-indexed union inside ZF.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D31](#st-d31), [ST-D33](#st-d33)
uses [ST-D31](#st-d31), [ST-D33](#st-d33)
proved-using [ST-A09](#st-a09), [ST-A08](#st-a08), [ST-T25](#st-t25).

nodes.label: Mostowski collapse theorem
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** If $R$ is a well-founded extensional relation on a set $A$, there are a unique transitive set $M$ and a unique bijection $\pi\colon A\to M$ with $xRy$ iff $\pi(x)\in\pi(y)$. The recursive equation is $\pi(x)=\{\pi(y):yRx\}$.

nodes.label: Well-founded recursion
nodes.statement:
**Background: ZF; schema.** Let $R$ be a well-founded relation on a set $A$. Given a definable rule $G$ assigning a unique set to $(x,h)$ whenever $x\in A$ and $h$ is a function on $\{y\in A:yRx\}$, there is a unique function $F$ on $A$ with

$$F(x)=G\bigl(x,F|_{\{y\in A:yRx\}}\bigr).$$

nodes.label: Cantor's theorem
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** There is no surjection $A\to\mathcal P(A)$. For a proposed $f$, the subset $D=\{a\in A:a\notin f(a)\}$ is outside its range. Since $a\mapsto\{a\}$ is injective, $A\prec\mathcal P(A)$.

nodes.label: Uncountability of the continuum
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** $\mathcal P(\omega)$ and $\{0,1\}^{\omega}$ are equipotent and uncountable. With the usual construction of the real numbers, $\mathbb R\simeq\mathcal P(\omega)$: rational cuts give one injection, ternary expansions using digits $0,2$ give the other. Thus in ZFC $|\mathbb R|=2^{\aleph_0}>\aleph_0$. Real-number constructions will be separate analysis entries.

nodes.label: Infinite cardinal addition and multiplication
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC.** For infinite cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$, $\kappa+\lambda=\kappa\lambda=\max(\kappa,\lambda)$. The assertion $\kappa\cdot\kappa=\kappa$ for infinite initial ordinals is already provable in ZF; choice extends the conclusion to the sizes of arbitrary infinite sets.

nodes.label: König's theorem
nodes.statement:
**Background: ZFC.** For set-indexed families of cardinals satisfying $\kappa_i<\lambda_i$ for every $i\in I$,

$$\sum_{i\in I}\kappa_i<\prod_{i\in I}\lambda_i.$$

Its diagonal argument bounds the possible behaviour of infinite cardinal exponentiation.

nodes.label: Cofinality of a power-set cardinal
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC.** For every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, $\mathrm{cf}(2^\kappa)>\kappa$. In particular the continuum cannot have countable cofinality. This restricts its possible cardinality without determining it.

nodes.label: Ultrafilter lemma
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; a weaker choice principle suffices.** Every proper filter on a set extends to an ultrafilter. Zorn's lemma proves this by ordering its proper filter extensions by inclusion; unions of chains remain proper filters. Over ZF the general extension assertion is equivalent to the Boolean prime ideal theorem and is strictly weaker than AC, in the usual relative-consistency sense.

nodes.label: Ultrafilter alternative
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** A proper filter $\mathcal U$ on $X$ is an ultrafilter iff for every $A\subseteq X$, exactly one of $A$ and $X\setminus A$ belongs to $\mathcal U$.

nodes.label: Hausdorff maximal principle
nodes.statement: **Background: ZFC; equivalent to AC over ZF.** Every chain in a partially ordered set is contained in a chain maximal under inclusion.

direct_dependencies.note: uses [ST-D22](#st-d22)

nodes.label: Comparability and rigidity within an ordinal
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** Every order automorphism of an ordinal is the identity. More generally a well-ordered set has no nontrivial order automorphism, and no well-order is isomorphic to one of its proper initial segments.

nodes.label: Products as universal constructions
nodes.statement: **Background: ZF.** For a family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$, its product has projections $p_i(f)=f(i)$. Given a set $X$ and maps $g_i\colon X\to A_i$, there is a unique $g\colon X\to\prod_i A_i$ satisfying $p_i\circ g=g_i$ for every $i$. This holds also for empty products and does not assert that every product of nonempty factors has an element.

nodes.label: Continuum hypothesis (CH) / Hypothèse du continu
nodes.statement: **Status:** Additional hypothesis over ZFC. $2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_1$. In ZFC this is equivalent to the absence of a cardinal strictly between the size of $\omega$ and the size of $\mathbb R$. ZFC proves neither CH nor its negation if ZFC is consistent.

nodes.label: Generalized continuum hypothesis (GCH)
nodes.statement: **Status:** Additional hypothesis over ZFC. For every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, $2^\kappa=\kappa^+$, where $\kappa^+$ is the least larger cardinal. This implies CH.

nodes.label: Gödel's constructibility and relative consistency theorem
nodes.statement:
**Kind:** Metatheorem, with an internal theorem schema. ZF proves, for each axiom, that the constructible class $L$ satisfies ZFC + GCH. Consequently,

$$\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZF})\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}+\mathrm{GCH}).$$

This supplies a relative consistency result; it does not prove that ZF itself is consistent.

nodes.label: Gödel–Cohen independence of CH
nodes.statement: **Kind:** Metatheorem. If ZFC is consistent, both ZFC + CH and ZFC + $\neg$CH are consistent. The positive direction follows from constructibility; Cohen's forcing method supplies the negative direction. Hence CH is independent of ZFC under this assumption. Since GCH implies CH, these results also give independence of GCH.
nodes.reference: [J](#bib-j), ch. 13–15. Forcing will have its own definition and theorem entries in a later instalment.

bibliography.locator: ch. 13–15. Forcing will have its own definition and theorem entries in a later instalment.

nodes.label: Independence of the axiom of choice from ZF
nodes.statement: **Kind:** Metatheorem. If ZF is consistent, both ZF + AC and ZF + $\neg$AC are consistent. Constructibility gives the first direction; constructions of symmetric models give the second. The claim concerns ZF with pure sets, so a result only about a theory with atoms would require a further transfer argument.

nodes.label: Usual scalar topology
nodes.statement: For $K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, set $B(a,r)=\{z:|z-a|<r\}$ for $r>0$. A set is open when each of its points lies in a ball contained in it. These balls define the usual topology on $K$.

nodes.label: Scalar sequences and subsequences
nodes.statement: A scalar sequence is a map $u:\mathbb N\to K$. A subsequence is $(u_{n_k})$ with strictly increasing indices. Convergence to $l$ means that for each $\varepsilon>0$, eventually $|u_n-l|<\varepsilon$.

nodes.label: Cauchy sequence
nodes.statement: A scalar sequence is Cauchy if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N$ such that $|u_n-u_m|<\varepsilon$ for all $m,n\ge N$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Algebra and uniqueness of sequence limits
nodes.statement: A convergent scalar sequence has a unique limit and is bounded. Sums and products of convergent sequences converge to the sum and product of the limits; quotients do so when the denominator limit is nonzero. Every subsequence has the same limit.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Monotone convergence for real sequences
nodes.statement: An increasing real sequence bounded above converges to the supremum of its values. A decreasing sequence bounded below converges to its infimum.

nodes.label: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
nodes.statement: Every bounded sequence in $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ has a convergent subsequence. For complex sequences apply the real result successively to the two coordinates.

nodes.label: Completeness of the scalar fields
nodes.statement: A sequence in $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ converges if and only if it is Cauchy. A Cauchy sequence is bounded; a convergent subsequence and the Cauchy condition give convergence of the full sequence.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Limit superior and limit inferior
nodes.statement: In $\overline{\mathbb R}=\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$, define $\limsup u_n=\inf_N\sup_{n\ge N}u_n$ and $\liminf u_n=\sup_N\inf_{n\ge N}u_n$, using extended bounds.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Characterisation by upper and lower limits
nodes.statement: For a real sequence, $\liminf u_n\le\limsup u_n$. It converges to a finite $l$ exactly when both equal $l$. For a bounded sequence these bounds are respectively its smallest and largest subsequential limits.

nodes.label: Scalar series
nodes.statement: The series $\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n$ converges to $s$ when its partial sums $s_N=\sum_{n=0}^N a_n$ converge to $s$. It converges absolutely when $\sum |a_n|$ converges; it converges conditionally when it converges but not absolutely.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy criterion and term test for series
nodes.statement: A scalar series converges exactly when for every $\varepsilon>0$ all sufficiently late finite tails have modulus below $\varepsilon$. Convergence implies $a_n\to0$; this necessary condition is not sufficient.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Comparison and absolute convergence
nodes.statement: If $|a_n|\le b_n$ eventually, with $b_n\ge0$ and $\sum b_n<\infty$, then $\sum a_n$ converges absolutely and converges. For nonnegative terms, the sum is the supremum of the partial sums, possibly $+\infty$.

nodes.label: Geometric series
nodes.statement: For $|q|<1$, $\sum_{n=0}^\infty q^n=(1-q)^{-1}$. For $|q|\ge1$ the terms fail to tend to zero.

nodes.label: Root and ratio tests
nodes.statement: For $L=\limsup |a_n|^{1/n}$, the series converges absolutely if $L<1$ and diverges if $L>1$. If terms are eventually nonzero, the ratio test gives absolute convergence when $\limsup |a_{n+1}/a_n|<1$ and divergence when $\liminf |a_{n+1}/a_n|>1$. Equality to one is inconclusive.

nodes.label: Alternating series test
nodes.statement: If $b_n\ge0$ decreases to zero, $\sum_{n=0}^\infty(-1)^n b_n$ converges and the error after term $N$ has modulus at most $b_{N+1}$.

nodes.label: Rearrangement of absolutely convergent series
nodes.statement: If $\sum a_n$ is absolutely convergent and $\pi$ is a permutation of $\mathbb N$, then $\sum a_{\pi(n)}$ converges absolutely to the same sum.

nodes.label: Pointwise and uniform convergence
nodes.statement: For maps $f_n:X\to K$, pointwise convergence to $f$ means $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ for every $x$. Uniform convergence means that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N$ such that $|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\varepsilon$ for all $x\in X$ and $n\ge N$. A function series converges uniformly when its partial sums do.

nodes.label: Uniform Cauchy criterion
nodes.statement: A sequence of scalar functions converges uniformly exactly when for every $\varepsilon>0$ all sufficiently late pairs satisfy $|f_n(x)-f_m(x)|<\varepsilon$ for every $x$.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Weierstrass M-test
nodes.statement: If $|f_n(x)|\le M_n$ for every $x$, where $M_n\ge0$ and $\sum M_n<\infty$, then $\sum f_n$ converges uniformly and absolutely at every point.

nodes.label: Power series and radius of convergence
nodes.statement: A power series centred at $a\in K$ has the form $\sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n(z-a)^n$. Its radius is $R=\sup\{r\ge0:\sum |c_n|r^n<\infty\}$, allowing $R=+\infty$.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy–Hadamard formula
nodes.statement: The radius of a power series satisfies $R^{-1}=\limsup |c_n|^{1/n}$, with $1/0=+\infty$ and $1/(+\infty)=0$. The series converges absolutely for $|z-a|<R$, diverges for $|z-a|>R$, and converges uniformly on every closed disc $|z-a|\le r<R$. No boundary convergence is asserted.

nodes.label: Scalar function limits and continuity
nodes.statement: For $f:A\subset K\to K$ and an accumulation point $a$ of $A$, $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=l$ means: for every $\varepsilon>0$ some $\delta>0$ makes $0<|x-a|<\delta$, $x\in A$, imply $|f(x)-l|<\varepsilon$. Continuity at $a\in A$ uses $|x-a|<\delta$ without the puncture and $l=f(a)$.

nodes.label: Sequential criterion for scalar limits
nodes.statement: The limit of $f$ at an accumulation point $a$ is $l$ exactly when $f(x_n)\to l$ for every sequence in $A\setminus\{a\}$ tending to $a$. The corresponding unpunctured condition characterises continuity.

nodes.label: Intermediate value theorem
nodes.statement: If $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, it assumes every value between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$.

nodes.label: Extreme value theorem
nodes.statement: A continuous real-valued function on a nonempty closed bounded real interval is bounded and attains its minimum and maximum.

nodes.label: Uniform continuity
nodes.statement: A map $f:A\subset K\to K$ is uniformly continuous if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that $|x-y|<\delta$ implies $|f(x)-f(y)|<\varepsilon$ for all $x,y\in A$.

nodes.label: Heine–Cantor theorem on an interval
nodes.statement: A continuous scalar-valued function on a closed bounded real interval is uniformly continuous.

nodes.label: Uniform limit theorem
nodes.statement: If continuous scalar functions on a topological space converge uniformly, their limit is continuous.

nodes.label: Derivative of a function of a real variable
nodes.statement: For $f:I\to K$, with $I$ an open real interval, the derivative is $f\prime(x)=\lim_{h\to0}(f(x+h)-f(x))/h$, if this limit exists. Higher derivatives are defined recursively; $f\in C^k(I)$ means derivatives through order $k$ exist and are continuous.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Differentiation rules
nodes.statement: Differentiability implies continuity. Sums and products satisfy $(f+g)\prime=f\prime+g\prime$ and $(fg)\prime=f\prime g+fg\prime$; $(f/g)\prime=(f\prime g-fg\prime)/g^2$ where $g\ne0$. For a real-valued differentiable inner function $g$ and a scalar-valued differentiable outer function $f$, $(f\circ g)\prime=(f\prime\circ g)g\prime$.

nodes.label: Fermat stationary point theorem
nodes.statement: If a real-valued function is differentiable at an interior local maximum or minimum, its derivative there is zero.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Rolle and mean value theorems
nodes.statement: If $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and differentiable on $(a,b)$, with $a<b$, there is $c\in(a,b)$ such that $f(b)-f(a)=f\prime(c)(b-a)$. In particular, equal endpoint values give $f\prime(c)=0$. The real-valued hypothesis is essential to this conclusion.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Derivative and monotonicity
nodes.statement: For a real differentiable function on an interval, $f\prime\ge0$ implies that $f$ is nondecreasing; $f\prime>0$ implies strict increase; $f\prime=0$ everywhere implies constancy.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Taylor theorem with Lagrange remainder
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be real-valued and $C^{n+1}$ on an open interval containing $a$ and $x$, with $x\ne a$. There exists $\xi$ strictly between them such that $f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n f^{(k)}(a)(x-a)^k/k!+f^{(n+1)}(\xi)(x-a)^{n+1}/(n+1)!$.

nodes.label: One-variable inverse differentiation
nodes.statement: If $f:I\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$ on an open interval and $f\prime$ never vanishes, then $f$ is one-to-one, $f(I)$ is an open interval, and its inverse is $C^1$ with $(f^{-1})\prime(y)=1/f\prime(f^{-1}(y))$.

nodes.label: Darboux sums and Riemann integral
nodes.statement: For bounded $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ and partition $a=x_0<\cdots<x_n=b$, define lower and upper sums by summing $(x_i-x_{i-1})\inf_{[x_{i-1},x_i]}f$ and the corresponding supremum. The lower integral is the supremum of lower sums and the upper integral is the infimum of upper sums. Equality defines Riemann integrability and $\int_a^b f$. Complex integrals are defined by integrating the real and imaginary parts; reverse endpoints negate the integral.

nodes.label: Integrability criterion and continuous functions
nodes.statement: A bounded real function is Riemann integrable exactly when for every $\varepsilon>0$ some partition has upper sum minus lower sum below $\varepsilon$. Continuous scalar functions on a closed bounded interval are Riemann integrable.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Elementary integral properties
nodes.statement: Riemann integration is linear and additive over adjacent intervals. For integrable real $f\le g$, $\int f\le\int g$. If scalar $f$ is integrable, so is $|f|$ and $|\int_a^b f|\le\int_a^b|f|$ for $a\le b$.

nodes.label: Primitive
nodes.statement: A primitive of $f:I\to K$ is a differentiable function $F:I\to K$ satisfying $F\prime=f$ on the real interval $I$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Fundamental theorem of calculus
nodes.statement: If $f:[a,b]\to K$ is continuous, $F(x)=\int_a^x f(t)\,dt$ satisfies $F\prime=f$ on $(a,b)$. If $F$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b F\prime(t)\,dt=F(b)-F(a)$.

nodes.label: Integration by parts and substitution
nodes.statement: For scalar $C^1$ functions $u,v$, $\int_a^b uv\prime=[uv]_a^b-\int_a^b u\prime v$. For continuous scalar $f$ on an interval containing the image of a real $C^1$ map $\phi:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, $\int_a^b f(\phi(t))\phi\prime(t)\,dt=\int_{\phi(a)}^{\phi(b)} f(s)\,ds$.

nodes.label: Integration of a uniform limit
nodes.statement: If Riemann integrable scalar functions $f_n$ on $[a,b]$ converge uniformly to $f$, then $f$ is Riemann integrable and $\int f_n\to\int f$. Consequently a uniformly convergent series of continuous functions can be integrated term by term on this interval.

nodes.label: Improper Riemann integral
nodes.statement: For locally Riemann integrable $f:[a,\infty)\to K$, define $\int_a^\infty f=\lim_{b\to\infty}\int_a^b f$ when this limit exists finitely. A singular finite endpoint is treated by a one-sided limit. With two improper endpoints the two limits must exist separately; their sum defines the integral. Absolute convergence means finiteness of the corresponding integral of $|f|$.

nodes.label: Absolute convergence of improper integrals
nodes.statement: An absolutely convergent improper scalar Riemann integral converges. If $|f|\le g$ near an improper endpoint, with $g\ge0$ and $\int g<\infty$, then the integral of $f$ converges absolutely, assuming local Riemann integrability.

nodes.label: Integral test and p-series
nodes.statement: For nonnegative decreasing continuous $f:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$, $\sum_{n=1}^\infty f(n)$ converges if and only if $\int_1^\infty f(x)\,dx$ converges. In particular $\sum n^{-p}$ converges exactly for real $p>1$.

nodes.label: Differentiation of power series
nodes.statement: Inside its radius of convergence a real or complex power series is differentiable term by term, with derivative $\sum_{n\ge1} n c_n(z-a)^{n-1}$. The derivative series has the same radius. Iterating gives $c_n=f^{(n)}(a)/n!$. In the complex case differentiation is in the complex sense.

nodes.label: Exponential and trigonometric functions
nodes.statement: Define $\exp z=\sum_{n\ge0}z^n/n!$, $\cos z=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n z^{2n}/(2n)!$, and $\sin z=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n z^{2n+1}/(2n+1)!$ for $z\in\mathbb C$. All three series have infinite radius of convergence.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Elementary function identities
nodes.statement: For complex $z,w$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$, $\exp z\ne0$, and $\exp(iz)=\cos z+i\sin z$. Their derivatives satisfy $\exp\prime=\exp$, $\sin\prime=\cos$, $\cos\prime=-\sin$. On the real line, $\exp$ is strictly increasing and maps onto $(0,\infty)$.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Real logarithm and real powers
nodes.statement: The logarithm $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse of the real exponential. For $x>0$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define $x^\alpha=\exp(\alpha\log x)$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Logarithm and power differentiation
nodes.statement: For $x,y>0$, $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$, $(\log x)\prime=1/x$, and $(x^\alpha)\prime=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ for fixed real $\alpha$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Holomorphic function
nodes.statement: For open $U\subset\mathbb C$, a function $f:U\to\mathbb C$ is holomorphic if $f\prime(z)=\lim_{h\to0,\ h\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}}(f(z+h)-f(z))/h$ exists at each $z\in U$. An entire function is holomorphic on all of $\mathbb C$. A domain is a nonempty connected open subset of $\mathbb C$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Analytic function
nodes.statement: A scalar function on an open subset of $K$ is analytic if near each point it equals a convergent power series centred at that point. Real analyticity and complex analyticity use real and complex neighbourhoods respectively.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Contour and contour integral
nodes.statement: A contour is a piecewise $C^1$ map $\gamma:[a,b]\to\mathbb C$. It is closed if $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. For continuous $f$ on its image, define $\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz=\int_a^b f(\gamma(t))\gamma\prime(t)\,dt$, adding the integrals over the finitely many smooth pieces. Its length is $L(\gamma)=\int_a^b|\gamma\prime(t)|\,dt$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Contour integral estimate
nodes.statement: For continuous $f$ on a contour $\gamma$, $|\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz|\le L(\gamma)\sup_{z\in\gamma([a,b])}|f(z)|$. Contour integrals are additive under concatenation and change sign under reversal.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Holomorphic primitive
nodes.statement: A holomorphic primitive of $f:U\to\mathbb C$ is a holomorphic function $F$ on $U$ with $F\prime=f$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Complex primitive theorem
nodes.statement: If $F$ is a holomorphic primitive of continuous $f$ on $U$ and $\gamma$ is a contour in $U$, then $\int_\gamma f=F(\gamma(b))-F(\gamma(a))$. In particular the integral on every closed contour vanishes.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy–Goursat theorem for triangles
nodes.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic on an open neighbourhood of a closed triangle and its interior, then $\int_{\partial\Delta}f(z)\,dz=0$, with positively oriented boundary. No continuity of the derivative is assumed.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy integral formula on a disc
nodes.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed disc $\overline{B(a,r)}$, then for $|z-a|<r$, $f(z)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{|\zeta-a|=r}f(\zeta)/(\zeta-z)\,d\zeta$, with counterclockwise orientation.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Holomorphic functions are analytic
nodes.statement: A holomorphic function has derivatives of every order and equals its Taylor series on each disc centred at $a$ whose closure lies in its domain. For a surrounding circle of radius $r$, $f^{(n)}(a)=n!/(2\pi i)\int_{|\zeta-a|=r}f(\zeta)/(\zeta-a)^{n+1}\,d\zeta$. Conversely, an analytic complex function is holomorphic.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy estimates
nodes.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic near $\overline{B(a,r)}$ and $|f|\le M$ on its boundary, then $|f^{(n)}(a)|\le n!M/r^n$ for each integer $n\ge0$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Identity theorem and isolated zeros
nodes.statement: A holomorphic function on a domain which is not identically zero has isolated zeros, each of finite positive order. If two holomorphic functions on a domain agree on a set with an accumulation point in that domain, they agree everywhere.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Maximum modulus principle
nodes.statement: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a domain has no local maximum of its modulus. Consequently a function continuous on the closure of a bounded domain and holomorphic inside attains its maximum modulus on the boundary.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Liouville theorem
nodes.statement: Every bounded entire function is constant: Cauchy estimates with arbitrarily large radii force its derivative to vanish.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Locally uniform convergence
nodes.statement: Functions on an open set $U\subset\mathbb C$ converge locally uniformly if they converge uniformly on each compact subset of $U$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Weierstrass convergence theorem
nodes.statement: A locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions on $U$ is holomorphic. Their derivatives of every fixed order converge locally uniformly to the corresponding derivative of the limit.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Morera theorem
nodes.statement: If $f$ is continuous on an open set $U\subset\mathbb C$ and its integral around every triangle whose closed interior lies in $U$ is zero, then $f$ is holomorphic on $U$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Winding number
nodes.statement: For a closed contour $\gamma$ and $a$ outside its image, define $\operatorname{Ind}(\gamma,a)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_\gamma dz/(z-a)$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Winding number properties
nodes.statement: The index of a closed contour is integer-valued and locally constant on the complement of the contour image, and is zero on the unbounded component. A counterclockwise circle has index one inside and zero outside.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Simply connected plane domain
nodes.statement: A plane domain is simply connected if every continuous closed path in it can be contracted to a point through continuous closed paths staying in the domain. Formally the homotopy is a continuous map $H:[0,1]^2\to U$ with $H(0,t)=H(1,t)$, prescribed initial path and constant final path. This is a topological construction, not multivariable differentiation.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Cauchy theorem on simply connected domains
nodes.statement: Every holomorphic function on a simply connected plane domain has a holomorphic primitive; its integral on each closed contour in the domain is zero.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Holomorphic logarithm
nodes.statement: A holomorphic logarithm of a nowhere zero function $f$ on $U$ is a holomorphic $g$ satisfying $\exp g=f$. A branch of the logarithm on $U\subset\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ is a logarithm of the identity function.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Existence of a holomorphic logarithm
nodes.statement: Every nowhere zero holomorphic function on a simply connected domain admits a holomorphic logarithm. One obtains it from a primitive of $f\prime/f$ and a suitable additive constant. There is no holomorphic logarithm of the identity on all of $\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Laurent series
nodes.statement: A Laurent series centred at $a$ is $\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}c_n(z-a)^n$, meaning the sum of its nonnegative-power and negative-power series wherever both converge. The negative-power part is the principal part.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Laurent expansion theorem
nodes.statement: A holomorphic function on an annulus $r<|z-a|<R$ has a unique Laurent expansion there, converging absolutely at each point and uniformly on compact subannuli. For $r<\rho<R$, $c_n=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{|\zeta-a|=\rho} f(\zeta)/(\zeta-a)^{n+1}\,d\zeta$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Isolated singularities and meromorphic functions
nodes.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic on a punctured neighbourhood of $a$, the singularity is removable if $f$ extends holomorphically across $a$; a pole of order $m\ge1$ if $(z-a)^m f(z)$ extends with nonzero value at $a$; otherwise it is essential. A meromorphic function on an open set is holomorphic except at a discrete set of poles with no accumulation inside that set.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Classification of isolated singularities
nodes.statement: An isolated singularity is removable exactly when all negative Laurent coefficients vanish, equivalently when $f$ is bounded near the puncture. It is a pole of order $m$ exactly when its principal part ends in a nonzero coefficient of $(z-a)^{-m}$. It is essential exactly when infinitely many negative coefficients are nonzero.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Residue
nodes.statement: The residue $\operatorname{Res}(f,a)$ at an isolated singularity is the coefficient of $(z-a)^{-1}$ in the Laurent expansion.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Residue theorem
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic on a simply connected domain $U$ except at finitely many isolated singularities $a_1,\ldots,a_m$. For any closed contour $\gamma$ in $U$ avoiding them, $\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz=2\pi i\sum_j\operatorname{Ind}(\gamma,a_j)\operatorname{Res}(f,a_j)$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Residue at a pole
nodes.statement: For a simple pole, $\operatorname{Res}(f,a)=\lim_{z\to a}(z-a)f(z)$. For a pole of order $m$, it equals $1/(m-1)!$ times the $(m-1)$st derivative at $a$ of the holomorphic extension of $(z-a)^m f(z)$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Argument principle
nodes.statement: If $f$ is meromorphic near a closed disc and has neither zeros nor poles on its boundary, then $(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{\partial B} f\prime(z)/f(z)\,dz=N-P$, where zeros and poles inside are counted with their orders and the boundary is counterclockwise.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Rouché theorem
nodes.statement: If $f,g$ are holomorphic near a closed disc and $|g|<|f|$ on its boundary, then $f$ and $f+g$ have the same number of zeros inside, counted with multiplicity.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Open mapping theorem
nodes.statement: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a domain maps open subsets to open subsets of $\mathbb C$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Schwarz lemma
nodes.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic on the unit disc, $|f|\le1$ and $f(0)=0$, then $|f(z)|\le|z|$ and $|f\prime(0)|\le1$. Equality at a nonzero point, or equality for the derivative bound, forces $f(z)=cz$ with $|c|=1$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient in the stated formulation.

nodes.label: Whole-set axiom for a σ-algebra
nodes.statement: A proposed $\sigma$-algebra $\Sigma$ on $X$ contains $X$.

nodes.label: Closure under complements
nodes.statement: If $A\in\Sigma$, then $X\setminus A\in\Sigma$.

nodes.label: Closure under countable unions
nodes.statement: For every sequence $(A_n)_{n\ge1}$ in $\Sigma$, $\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\Sigma$.

nodes.label: σ-algebra / Tribu
nodes.statement: A $\sigma$-algebra on $X$ is a family $\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal P(X)$ satisfying MT-A01–MT-A03. Its members are called measurable sets relative to $\Sigma$. A topology alone is not generally a $\sigma$-algebra.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Measurable space / Espace mesurable
nodes.statement: A measurable space is a pair $(X,\Sigma)$ consisting of a set and a specified $\sigma$-algebra on it. Neither a measure nor a topology is part of this pair.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Generated σ-algebra / Tribu engendrée
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P(X)$, $\sigma_X(\mathcal C)$ is the intersection of all $\sigma$-algebras on $X$ containing $\mathcal C$. It is the smallest such $\sigma$-algebra.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Trace σ-algebra / Tribu induite
nodes.statement: For $A\subseteq X$, define $\Sigma|_A=\{A\cap B:B\in\Sigma\}$. This is a $\sigma$-algebra on $A$, whether or not $A\in\Sigma$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Measurable mapping / Application mesurable
nodes.statement: A map $f:(X,\Sigma)\to(Y,\mathcal T)$ is measurable if $f^{-1}(B)\in\Sigma$ for every $B\in\mathcal T$. Its measurability depends on both specified $\sigma$-algebras.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Borel σ-algebra / Tribu borélienne
nodes.statement: For a topological space $(E,\tau)$, its Borel $\sigma$-algebra is $\mathcal B(E)=\sigma_E(\tau)$. Members are Borel sets. The pair $(E,\mathcal B(E))$ is its Borel measurable space. No measure is introduced by this construction.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Usual real topology and real Borel structure
nodes.statement: On $\mathbb R$, the usual topology consists of unions of open intervals $(a,b)=\{x:a<x<b\}$. Rational-endpoint open intervals give a countable basis. Its generated $\sigma$-algebra is the usual $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Product σ-algebra
nodes.statement: For measurable spaces $(X,\Sigma)$ and $(Y,\mathcal T)$, $\Sigma\otimes\mathcal T$ is the $\sigma$-algebra on $X\times Y$ generated by rectangles $A\times B$ with $A\in\Sigma$, $B\in\mathcal T$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Sub-σ-algebra
nodes.statement: A sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$ is a $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal G$ on the same set $X$ with $\mathcal G\subseteq\Sigma$. For a measurable map $f:X\to(Y,\mathcal T)$, $\sigma(f)=\{f^{-1}(B):B\in\mathcal T\}$ is the smallest $\sigma$-algebra making $f$ measurable.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Elementary closure properties of a σ-algebra
nodes.statement: A $\sigma$-algebra contains $\varnothing$ and is closed under countable intersections, finite unions and intersections, differences and symmetric differences.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Existence and universal property of generated σ-algebras
nodes.statement: Intersections of $\sigma$-algebras on a fixed set are $\sigma$-algebras. Since $\mathcal P(X)$ is one, $\sigma_X(\mathcal C)$ exists for every $\mathcal C$. If $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal T$ is a $\sigma$-algebra, then $\sigma_X(\mathcal C)\subseteq\mathcal T$.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Inverse-image σ-algebras and traces
nodes.statement: For any set map $f:X\to Y$ and $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal T$ on $Y$, the family $f^{-1}(\mathcal T)=\{f^{-1}(B):B\in\mathcal T\}$ is a $\sigma$-algebra. In particular the trace $\Sigma|_A$ is a $\sigma$-algebra on $A$.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Composition of measurable maps
nodes.statement: Identity maps are measurable. The composite of measurable maps is measurable when the intermediate space carries the same $\sigma$-algebra for both maps.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Testing measurability on generators
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal T=\sigma_Y(\mathcal C)$, then $f:(X,\Sigma)\to(Y,\mathcal T)$ is measurable exactly when $f^{-1}(C)\in\Sigma$ for every $C\in\mathcal C$.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Continuous maps are Borel measurable
nodes.statement: A continuous map $f:E\to F$ between topological spaces is measurable from $(E,\mathcal B(E))$ to $(F,\mathcal B(F))$. The converse need not hold.

nodes.label: Borel structure of a subspace
nodes.statement: For any subset $A$ of a topological space $E$, $\mathcal B(A)=\mathcal B(E)|_A$ when $A$ has the subspace topology. This does not require $A$ itself to be Borel in $E$.

nodes.label: Generators of the real Borel σ-algebra
nodes.statement: $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$ is generated by open intervals with rational endpoints, and also by rays $(-\infty,a)$ or $(-\infty,a]$ with $a\in\mathbb Q$. Thus real-valued measurability can be tested on these rays.

nodes.label: Nonnegative extended reals and their measurable structure
nodes.statement: $[0,+\infty]$ is the nonnegative real half-line with a largest element $+\infty$ adjoined. Use $a+(+\infty)=+\infty$, $c(+\infty)=+\infty$ for $c>0$, and $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$; $+\infty-(+\infty)$ is undefined. Its measurable structure is generated by the sets $\{t:t>a\}$, $a\ge0$. Every subset has a supremum in this ordered set, with $\sup\varnothing=0$.

nodes.label: Nonnegative series and monotone limits
nodes.statement: For $a_n\in[0,+\infty]$, define $\sum_{n\ge1}a_n=\sup_N\sum_{n=1}^N a_n$. An increasing sequence in this ordered set has limit its supremum; a decreasing sequence has limit its infimum. These order conventions allow measure limits without introducing integration.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Indicator and measurable simple function
nodes.statement: The indicator $\mathbf1_A$ equals 1 on $A$ and 0 elsewhere. A measurable simple function is a real-valued measurable map with finite range; it can be written $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ using a finite measurable partition. No measure is needed.
