nodes.label: Coordinatewise measurability into a product
nodes.statement: A map $f:Z\to X\times Y$ is measurable for $\Sigma\otimes\mathcal T$ exactly when both coordinate maps are measurable. For every product-measurable set, each section at a fixed coordinate is measurable in the other space.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Borel product comparison
nodes.statement: For arbitrary topological spaces $E,F$, $\mathcal B(E)\otimes\mathcal B(F)\subseteq\mathcal B(E\times F)$ with the product topology. If both spaces have countable bases, equality holds: every product-open set is a countable union of basic open rectangles. Equality is not asserted for arbitrary spaces.

nodes.label: Countable pointwise operations preserve measurability
nodes.statement: For measurable $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$, the functions $\sup_n f_n$, $\inf_n f_n$, $\limsup_n f_n=\inf_N\sup_{n\ge N}f_n$ and $\liminf_n f_n=\sup_N\inf_{n\ge N}f_n$ are measurable. A pointwise limit, when it exists, is measurable. Finite real-valued sums, products, maxima and minima of real measurable functions are measurable.

nodes.label: Approximation by nonnegative simple functions
nodes.statement: Every measurable $f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ is the pointwise increasing limit of a sequence of nonnegative measurable simple functions. One may truncate at height $n$ and round down to multiples of $2^{-n}$. This assertion concerns measurability only.

nodes.label: Nonnegative values of a measure
nodes.statement: A proposed measure $\mu$ takes values in $[0,+\infty]$.

nodes.label: Empty-set measure
nodes.statement: A proposed measure satisfies $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. This is stated explicitly to exclude the identically infinite set function.

nodes.label: Countable additivity / σ-additivité
nodes.statement: For pairwise disjoint measurable sets $(A_n)_{n\ge1}$, $\mu(\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(A_n)$.

nodes.label: Measure / Mesure positive
nodes.statement: A measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ is a function $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfying MT-A04–MT-A06. All uses of measure in this catalogue mean a nonnegative countably additive measure; signed and complex measures are deferred.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Measure space / Espace mesuré
nodes.statement: A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $(X,\Sigma)$ is a measurable space and $\mu$ is a measure on it. Specifying only $(X,\Sigma)$ does not specify any masses.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Finite, probability and σ-finite measures
nodes.statement: A measure is finite if $\mu(X)<+\infty$, a probability measure if $\mu(X)=1$, and $\sigma$-finite if $X=\bigcup_{n\ge1}E_n$ with each $E_n\in\Sigma$ and $\mu(E_n)<+\infty$. Finite measures are $\sigma$-finite.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Null set and negligible subset
nodes.statement: A measurable set $N\in\Sigma$ is null if $\mu(N)=0$. A subset of a measurable null set is called negligible here; in an incomplete measure space it need not itself be measurable.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Almost everywhere / Presque partout
nodes.statement: A property holds $\mu$-almost everywhere if it fails only on a subset of some measurable null set. Functions agree almost everywhere if their equality holds in this sense. The exceptional subset need not be measurable under this convention.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Complete measure space / Espace mesuré complet
nodes.statement: A measure space is complete if every subset of a measurable null set belongs to its $\sigma$-algebra. By monotonicity all these subsets then have measure zero. Completeness here is unrelated to metric completeness.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Restriction of a measure
nodes.statement: For measurable $A\in\Sigma$, the restricted space is $(A,\Sigma|_A,\mu|_A)$, where $\mu|_A(B)=\mu(B)$ for $B\in\Sigma|_A$. Measurability of $A$ ensures these sets are in $\Sigma$. One may also restrict $\mu$ to a sub-$\sigma$-algebra on the same set.

nodes.label: Pushforward measure / Mesure image
nodes.statement: For a measurable map $f:(X,\Sigma)\to(Y,\mathcal T)$ and a measure $\mu$ on $X$, define $(f_*\mu)(B)=\mu(f^{-1}(B))$ for $B\in\mathcal T$. This is a measure on the specified codomain $\sigma$-algebra.

nodes.label: Borel measure / Mesure borélienne
nodes.statement: A Borel measure on a topological space $E$ is a measure on $(E,\mathcal B(E))$. It is not assumed finite, complete or regular. Radon conditions require additional hypotheses and are deferred.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dirac and counting measures
nodes.statement: For $x\in X$, the Dirac measure satisfies $\delta_x(A)=1$ if $x\in A$ and 0 otherwise. Counting measure assigns to a finite measurable set its cardinality and to an infinite measurable set $+\infty$. Both are defined on any specified $\sigma$-algebra on $X$; the zero measure assigns 0 to every measurable set.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Finite additivity, monotonicity and difference
nodes.statement: For disjoint measurable $A,B$, $\mu(A\cup B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B)$. If $A\subseteq B$ are measurable then $\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$. If moreover $\mu(A)<+\infty$, then $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$, allowing $\mu(B)=+\infty$. No subtraction $+\infty-(+\infty)$ is used.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Countable subadditivity
nodes.statement: For measurable sets $A_n$, $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$. Replace the family by disjoint successive differences and use countable additivity and monotonicity.

direct_dependencies.note: Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.
Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Continuity from below
nodes.statement: If $A_n\in\Sigma$ and $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$, then $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)=\sup_n\mu(A_n)=\lim_n\mu(A_n)$. No finiteness assumption is required.

nodes.label: Continuity from above
nodes.statement: If $A_n\in\Sigma$, $A_{n+1}\subseteq A_n$ and $\mu(A_1)<+\infty$, then $\mu(\bigcap_n A_n)=\inf_n\mu(A_n)=\lim_n\mu(A_n)$. The finite-measure hypothesis cannot be omitted in general.

nodes.label: Countable unions of null sets
nodes.statement: A countable union of measurable null sets is measurable and null. Every measurable subset of a null set is null. Consequently a countable collection of almost-everywhere assertions can hold simultaneously outside one measurable null set containing their exceptional subsets.

nodes.label: Restrictions and pushforwards are measures
nodes.statement: The restrictions and pushforwards defined above are countably additive measures. Pushforward preserves total mass and is compatible with composition: $(g\circ f)_*\mu=g_*(f_*\mu)$. In particular finite and probability measures remain such under pushforward. A pushforward of a σ-finite measure need not be σ-finite.

nodes.label: Completion of a measure space
nodes.statement: For $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$, let $\overline\Sigma^\mu$ consist of sets $A\subseteq X$ for which $B\subseteq A\subseteq C$ for some $B,C\in\Sigma$ with $\mu(C\setminus B)=0$. Define $\overline\mu(A)=\mu(B)$. The completion theorem makes this independent of the chosen pair and yields a complete extension.

nodes.label: Completion theorem
nodes.statement: The family $\overline\Sigma^\mu$ is a $\sigma$-algebra and $\overline\mu$ is a well-defined complete measure extending $\mu$. It is the unique measure on this $\sigma$-algebra extending $\mu$. Any complete extension on a larger $\sigma$-algebra contains this completion and agrees with its measure.

nodes.label: Algebra of subsets
nodes.statement: An algebra on $X$ is a family containing $X$ and closed under complements in $X$ and finite unions. It need not be closed under countable unions.

nodes.label: Monotone class of subsets
nodes.statement: A monotone class on $X$ is a family closed under unions of increasing sequences and intersections of decreasing sequences of its members.

Immediate concept or selected ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Monotone class theorem
nodes.statement: For an algebra $\mathcal A$ of subsets of $X$, the smallest monotone class containing $\mathcal A$ is $\sigma_X(\mathcal A)$.

nodes.label: Uniqueness of finite measures on a generating algebra
nodes.statement: If finite measures $\mu,\nu$ on $\sigma_X(\mathcal A)$ agree on an algebra $\mathcal A$, they agree on the whole generated $\sigma$-algebra. The equality class is a monotone class by continuity from below and above. Finiteness is used for decreasing intersections.

nodes.statement:
Let $\mu,
u$ be measures on $\sigma_X(\mathcal A)$ agreeing on an algebra $\mathcal A$. If there are $E_n\in\mathcal A$ covering $X$ with $\mu(E_n)=

nodes.label: Nonnegative sums of measures
nodes.statement: If $\mu_n$ are measures on the same measurable space and $c_n\in[0,+\infty)$, then $\nu(A)=\sum_{n\ge1}c_n\mu_n(A)$ is a measure, using $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$. Reordering a double series of nonnegative terms is justified by taking suprema over finite subsums; no integration theorem is needed.

nodes.label: Empty set and whole space are open
nodes.statement: For a proposed topology $\tau$ on a set $E$, $\varnothing\in\tau$ and $E\in\tau$.

nodes.label: Arbitrary unions of open sets
nodes.statement: For every family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of members of $\tau$, $\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i\in\tau$. The empty union is $\varnothing$.

nodes.label: Finite intersections of open sets
nodes.statement: The intersection of finitely many members of $\tau$ belongs to $\tau$. The empty intersection is $E$.

nodes.label: Topology and topological space / Topologie et espace topologique
nodes.statement: A topology on a set $E$ is a family $\tau\subseteq\mathcal P(E)$ satisfying TOP-A01–TOP-A03. Its members are the open subsets. The pair $(E,\tau)$ is a topological space. The first axiom is recorded separately for readability although the empty-family cases of the other two imply it.

nodes.label: Closed subset / Partie fermée
nodes.statement: A subset $F\subseteq E$ is closed in $(E,\tau)$ if $E\setminus F$ is open. A clopen subset is both open and closed. Closedness is relative to the specified ambient space; it is not an intrinsic extra condition on a space considered by itself.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Neighbourhood / Voisinage
nodes.statement: A neighbourhood of $x\in E$ is a subset $V\subseteq E$ containing an open set $U$ with $x\in U$. Write $\mathcal N_E(x)$ for all such $V$. A neighbourhood of a subset $A$ contains an open set containing $A$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Neighbourhood basis / Système fondamental de voisinages
nodes.statement: A neighbourhood basis at $x$ is a family $\mathcal B_x\subseteq\mathcal N_E(x)$ such that every neighbourhood of $x$ contains a member of $\mathcal B_x$. An open neighbourhood basis has only open members.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Basis and subbasis of a topology
nodes.statement: A basis $\mathcal B\subseteq\tau$ is a family whose unions give all open subsets. A subbasis $\mathcal S\subseteq\tau$ is a family whose finite intersections, including $E$, form a basis.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Interior / Intérieur
nodes.statement: The interior $\operatorname{Int}_E A$ is the union of all open subsets of $E$ contained in $A$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Closure / Adhérence
nodes.statement: The closure $\overline A^{\,E}$ is the intersection of all closed subsets of $E$ containing $A$. A point in this closure is adherent to $A$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Boundary / Frontière
nodes.statement: The boundary of $A\subseteq E$ is $\partial_E A=\overline A^{\,E}\setminus\operatorname{Int}_E A$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Dense and nowhere dense subsets
nodes.statement: $A\subseteq E$ is dense if $\overline A^{\,E}=E$, and nowhere dense if $\operatorname{Int}_E(\overline A^{\,E})=\varnothing$.

bibliography.locator: I, §1, no. 6; nowhere dense as associated terminology

Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Discrete, indiscrete and finer topologies
nodes.statement: The discrete topology on $E$ is $\mathcal P(E)$; the indiscrete topology is $\{\varnothing,E\}$. A topology $\tau_2$ is finer than $\tau_1$ if $\tau_1\subseteq\tau_2$; then $\tau_1$ is coarser.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Closed-set axioms
nodes.statement: The closed subsets contain $\varnothing,E$, are stable under arbitrary intersections and finite unions. Conversely any such family is the family of closed subsets of a unique topology, obtained by complementation.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Neighbourhood characterisation of a topology
nodes.statement: For each $x$, $\mathcal N_E(x)$ is a proper filter, each of whose members contains $x$. If $V\in\mathcal N_E(x)$, there is $W\in\mathcal N_E(x)$ such that $V\in\mathcal N_E(y)$ for every $y\in W$. Conversely, assigning to each $x$ a proper filter with these two properties determines a unique topology: $U$ is open exactly when $U\in\mathcal N_E(x)$ for every $x\in U$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Basis criterion and generated topology
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal B$ is a basis for a topology on $E$ exactly when it covers $E$ and, whenever $x\in B_1\cap B_2$ with $B_i\in\mathcal B$, some $B_3\in\mathcal B$ satisfies $x\in B_3\subseteq B_1\cap B_2$. Its unions form that topology. Every family of subsets generates a smallest topology, using finite intersections as a basis and then arbitrary unions.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Interior and closure by neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: $x\in\operatorname{Int}_E A$ exactly when $A$ is a neighbourhood of $x$. Also $x\in\overline A^{\,E}$ exactly when every neighbourhood of $x$ meets $A$. Hence $A$ is open exactly when $A=\operatorname{Int}_E A$, and closed exactly when $A=\overline A^{\,E}$.

nodes.label: Closure laws and complement duality
nodes.statement: Closure is extensive, monotone and idempotent, with $\overline\varnothing=\varnothing$ and $\overline{A\cup B}=\overline A\cup\overline B$. Moreover $E\setminus\overline A=\operatorname{Int}_E(E\setminus A)$. Interior is contractive, monotone and idempotent and preserves finite intersections.

nodes.label: Boundary and density criteria
nodes.statement: $\partial_E A=\overline A\cap\overline{E\setminus A}$ is closed. A point lies on this boundary exactly when each neighbourhood meets both $A$ and its complement. A subset is dense exactly when it meets every nonempty open subset.

nodes.label: Continuity at a point / Continuité en un point
nodes.statement: For $f:(E,\tau_E)\to(F,\tau_F)$ and $x\in E$, continuity at $x$ means: for every neighbourhood $V$ of $f(x)$ in $F$, $f^{-1}(V)$ is a neighbourhood of $x$ in $E$. Equivalently, some neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ satisfies $f(U)\subseteq V$. Both topologies are part of this assertion.

Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Continuous mapping / Application continue
nodes.statement: A map $f:(E,\tau_E)\to(F,\tau_F)$ is continuous if it is continuous at every point of $E$. Equivalently, the inverse image of each open subset of $F$ is open in $E$. This equivalence is recorded in TOP-T05.

nodes.label: Homeomorphism / Homéomorphisme
nodes.statement: A homeomorphism is a bijection between topological spaces for which both the map and its inverse are continuous.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Open and closed mappings
nodes.statement: A map between topological spaces is open if it sends every open subset to an open subset, and closed if it sends every closed subset to a closed subset. Neither property by itself asserts continuity.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Subspace topology / Topologie induite
nodes.statement: For $A\subseteq E$, the subspace topology is $\tau_A=\{A\cap U:U\in\tau_E\}$. Relative openness and relative closedness refer to this topology; a closed subset of $A$ need not be closed in $E$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Topological embedding / Plongement
nodes.statement: A map $f:E\to F$ is an embedding if it is a homeomorphism of $E$ onto the subspace $f(E)$ of $F$.

direct_dependencies.note: Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.
Selected immediate concept or proof ingredient for this formulation.

nodes.label: Initial topology / Topologie initiale
nodes.statement: Given maps $f_i:E\to F_i$ into topological spaces, the initial topology is the coarsest topology on $E$ making every $f_i$ continuous. It is generated by the subsets $f_i^{-1}(U)$ for $U$ open in $F_i$.

nodes.label: Final topology / Topologie finale
nodes.statement: Given maps $f_i:E_i\to F$ from topological spaces, the final topology is the finest topology on $F$ making every $f_i$ continuous: $U\subseteq F$ is open exactly when every $f_i^{-1}(U)$ is open in $E_i$.

nodes.label: Product topology / Topologie produit
nodes.statement: On $E=\prod_{i\in I}E_i$, the product topology is initial for the coordinate projections $\pi_i$. Basic opens restrict only finitely many coordinates: $\bigcap_{i\in J}\pi_i^{-1}(U_i)$ with $J\subseteq I$ finite. The empty product is a one-point space.

nodes.label: Quotient topology / Topologie quotient
nodes.statement: For a surjection $q:E\to Q$, the quotient topology is the final topology for $q$: $U\subseteq Q$ is open exactly when $q^{-1}(U)$ is open in $E$. In particular an equivalence relation gives this topology on its set of classes. A quotient map is a surjection for which the given codomain topology is this one.

nodes.label: Equivalent continuity criteria
nodes.statement: For $f:E\to F$, continuity at every point is equivalent to preservation of openness by inverse image, and to preservation of closedness by inverse image. It is also equivalent to $f(\overline A^{\,E})\subseteq\overline{f(A)}^{\,F}$ for every $A\subseteq E$.

nodes.label: Identity and composition of continuous maps
nodes.statement: Identity maps are continuous. Composites of continuous maps are continuous; more locally, continuity of $f$ at $x$ and of $g$ at $f(x)$ implies continuity of $g\circ f$ at $x$.

nodes.label: Finer topologies and continuity of identity
nodes.statement: For topologies $\tau_1,\tau_2$ on $E$, $\tau_2$ is finer than $\tau_1$ exactly when $\mathrm{id}:(E,\tau_2)\to(E,\tau_1)$ is continuous.

nodes.label: Subspace closure and continuity
nodes.statement: If $B\subseteq A\subseteq E$, then $\overline B^{\,A}=A\cap\overline B^{\,E}$. A map $g:X\to A$ is continuous exactly when its composite with the inclusion $A\hookrightarrow E$ is continuous. Restricting a continuous map to a subspace preserves continuity.

nodes.label: Universal properties of initial and final topologies
nodes.statement: For an initial topology on $E$ induced by $f_i:E\to F_i$, a map $g:X\to E$ is continuous exactly when every $f_i\circ g$ is continuous. For a final topology on $F$ induced by $f_i:E_i\to F$, a map $g:F\to Y$ is continuous exactly when every $g\circ f_i$ is continuous.

nodes.label: Coordinatewise continuity into a product
nodes.statement: A map $f:X\to\prod_i E_i$ is continuous exactly when each coordinate map $\pi_i\circ f$ is continuous.

nodes.label: Factorisation through a quotient space
nodes.statement: Let $q:E\to Q$ be a quotient map. A set map $h:Q\to F$ is continuous exactly when $h\circ q$ is continuous. Thus a continuous map on $E$ constant on each fibre of $q$ descends uniquely to a continuous map on $Q$.

nodes.label: Open or closed surjections are quotient maps
nodes.statement: A continuous surjection which is open or closed is a quotient map. Consequently a continuous bijection which is open or closed is a homeomorphism.

nodes.label: Pasting lemma
nodes.statement: If open subsets $U_i$ cover $E$ and continuous maps $f_i:U_i\to F$ agree on overlaps, the resulting map $E\to F$ is continuous. The same assertion holds for a finite closed cover.

nodes.label: Image filter / Filtre image
nodes.statement: For a map $f:E\to F$ and a proper filter $\mathcal F$ on $E$, its image filter is $f_*\mathcal F=\{B\subseteq F:f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F\}$. It is generated by the subsets $f(A)$ for $A\in\mathcal F$.

nodes.label: Convergence of a filter / Limite d’un filtre
nodes.statement: A proper filter $\mathcal F$ on a topological space $E$ converges to $x$ if $\mathcal N_E(x)\subseteq\mathcal F$. Thus every neighbourhood of $x$ belongs to the filter. A filter can have more than one limit unless separation is assumed.

nodes.label: Cluster point of a filter / Valeur d’adhérence
nodes.statement: A point $x$ is a cluster point of a proper filter $\mathcal F$ if every neighbourhood of $x$ meets every member of $\mathcal F$. Equivalently $x\in\bigcap_{A\in\mathcal F}\overline A$.

nodes.label: Limit of a function along a subset
nodes.statement: Let $A\subseteq E$, $a\in\overline A^{\,E}$ and $f:A\to F$. We write $f(x)\to b$ as $x\to a$ along $A$ if for each neighbourhood $V$ of $b$ there is a neighbourhood $U$ of $a$ with $f(A\cap U)\subseteq V$. This is the limit of the image of the trace-neighbourhood filter on $A$. For a punctured limit replace $A$ by $A\setminus\{a\}$ and require $a\in\overline{A\setminus\{a\}}$; the value at $a$ then has no effect.

nodes.label: Convergent sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $E$ converges to $x$ if every neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ contains every $x_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Equivalently its tail filter converges to $x$, where the tail filter consists of subsets containing some tail $\{x_n:n\ge N\}$.

nodes.label: Hausdorff space / Espace séparé
nodes.statement: A space is Hausdorff if distinct points have disjoint neighbourhoods. This condition is also called the $T_2$ separation axiom.

nodes.label: T₁ space
nodes.statement: A space is $T_1$ if every singleton is closed. This condition is weaker than being Hausdorff; it is not included in the definition of a topological space.

nodes.label: First-countable space
nodes.statement: A space is first-countable if every point has a countable neighbourhood basis. This local condition makes sequences sufficient for several tests that otherwise require filters.

nodes.label: Closure tested by convergent filters
nodes.statement: For $A\subseteq E$, $x\in\overline A$ exactly when some proper filter on $E$ containing $A$ converges to $x$. If $x\in\overline A$, the sets $A\cap V$, $V\in\mathcal N_E(x)$, generate such a filter. No choice principle is needed for this construction.

nodes.label: Cluster points and finer convergent filters
nodes.statement: A point $x$ is a cluster point of a proper filter $\mathcal F$ exactly when there exists a proper filter $\mathcal G\supseteq\mathcal F$ converging to $x$. For an ultrafilter, every cluster point is already a limit.

nodes.label: Continuity characterised by filters
nodes.statement: A map $f:E\to F$ is continuous at $x$ exactly when, for every proper filter $\mathcal F$ converging to $x$, the image filter $f_*\mathcal F$ converges to $f(x)$. The converse follows by testing the neighbourhood filter itself.

nodes.label: Continuous maps preserve limits
nodes.statement: If $f(x)\to b$ along a subset $A$ at an adherent point $a$, and $g$ is continuous at $b$, then $g(f(x))\to g(b)$ along the same approach. In particular continuous maps send convergent sequences to convergent sequences with the corresponding image limit.

nodes.label: Hausdorff criterion by uniqueness of limits
nodes.statement: A space is Hausdorff exactly when every proper filter has at most one limit. Consequently, in a Hausdorff codomain a function limit along a subset at an adherent point, and a sequential limit, are unique. The properness or adherence condition prevents vacuous convergence.

nodes.label: Hausdorff diagonal and T₁ property
nodes.statement: A space $E$ is Hausdorff exactly when its diagonal $\{(x,x):x\in E\}$ is closed in $E\times E$. Every Hausdorff space is $T_1$.

nodes.label: Subspaces and products preserve Hausdorffness
nodes.statement: Every subspace of a Hausdorff space is Hausdorff. An arbitrary product of Hausdorff spaces, with the product topology, is Hausdorff, including the empty product.

nodes.label: Equality on a dense subset
nodes.statement: If continuous maps $f,g:E\to F$ agree on a dense subset of $E$ and $F$ is Hausdorff, then $f=g$. The equaliser is closed, being the inverse image of the diagonal under $x\mapsto(f(x),g(x))$.

nodes.label: Filter convergence in a product
nodes.statement: A proper filter $\mathcal F$ on $\prod_i E_i$ converges to $x=(x_i)$ exactly when each image filter $(\pi_i)_*\mathcal F$ converges to $x_i$. The finite-coordinate basis makes the converse possible using finite intersections in the filter.

nodes.label: Sequences in first-countable spaces
nodes.statement: In a first-countable space, assuming countable choice, $x\in\overline A$ exactly when a sequence in $A$ converges to $x$. If the domain is first-countable, a map is continuous at $x$ exactly when it preserves all sequential limits at $x$; the converse also uses countable choice. These sequential tests need not hold in arbitrary topological spaces.

nodes.label: Continuity and punctured limits
nodes.statement: If $f:E\to F$ and $a$ is adherent to $E\setminus\{a\}$, then $f$ is continuous at $a$ exactly when its punctured limit at $a$ is $f(a)$. If $a$ is isolated, meaning $\{a\}$ is open, every map from $E$ is continuous at $a$; our punctured-limit convention excludes this vacuous approach.

nodes.label: Open cover and quasi-compactness / Quasi-compacité
nodes.statement: An open cover of $E$ is a family of open subsets whose union is $E$. The space is quasi-compact if every open cover has a finite subcover. A subset is quasi-compact when equipped with the subspace topology. No separation condition is imposed.

nodes.label: Compact space / Espace compact
nodes.statement: Following Bourbaki, a compact space is a Hausdorff quasi-compact space. A compact subset means a subset whose induced topology is compact. Many other authors use compact to mean only quasi-compact; the convention here always includes Hausdorffness.

nodes.label: Connected space / Espace connexe
nodes.statement: A space is connected if it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets. Equivalently its only clopen subsets are $\varnothing$ and the whole space. A connected subset is connected with the subspace topology. The empty space is connected under this convention.

nodes.label: Connected component / Composante connexe
nodes.statement: The connected component of a point $x$ is the largest connected subset containing $x$. It exists as the union of all connected subsets containing $x$.

nodes.label: Locally connected space
nodes.statement: A space is locally connected if each point has a neighbourhood basis consisting of connected open subsets.

nodes.label: Locally compact Hausdorff space
nodes.statement: A Hausdorff space is locally compact if each point has a compact neighbourhood, where the neighbourhood itself need not be open. In this Hausdorff setting one can equivalently require a neighbourhood basis of compact neighbourhoods.

nodes.label: Closed-set and filter tests for quasi-compactness
nodes.statement: A space is quasi-compact exactly when every family of closed sets with the finite intersection property has nonempty total intersection. The finite intersection property includes nonemptiness of the intersection of the empty subfamily, namely the ambient space. Equivalently every proper filter has a cluster point.

nodes.label: Ultrafilter test for quasi-compactness
nodes.statement: Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, a space is quasi-compact exactly when every ultrafilter on it converges to some point. Only the implication from ultrafilter convergence to quasi-compactness needs the extension principle.

nodes.label: Closed subsets of quasi-compact spaces
nodes.statement: A closed subspace of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact. Thus a closed subspace of a compact space is compact. Finite unions of quasi-compact subsets are quasi-compact.

nodes.label: Quasi-compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed
nodes.statement: If $K$ is a quasi-compact subset of a Hausdorff space $E$, then $K$ is closed in $E$. In particular compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed.

nodes.label: Continuous images and compact-to-Hausdorff bijections
nodes.statement: A continuous image of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact. Hence a continuous image of a compact space in a Hausdorff space is compact. A continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.

nodes.statement: In ZFC, any product of quasi-compact spaces is quasi-compact in the product topology. In particular any product of compact spaces is compact in the Bourbaki convention. nodes.label: Connected unions and components
nodes.statement: A family of connected subsets with a common point has connected union. Consequently each point lies in a unique connected component; components partition the space and are closed. Components need not be open.

nodes.statement: A space is locally connected exactly when the connected components of each open subspace are open in the whole space. In particular components of a locally connected space are open.

AS:B.title: Algebra I: Chapters 1–3
AS:B.citation: **[B] Nicolas Bourbaki, *Algebra I: Chapters 1–3*.** English translation, Hermann/Addison-Wesley, 1974; Springer reprint, 1989, softcover 1998, ISBN 978-3-540-64243-5. [Publisher record](https://link.springer.com/book/9783540642435); [university-hosted scan of the 1974 text](https://math.mit.edu/~hrm/palestine/bourbaki-algebra-1i.pdf). The chapter-I table of contents and the definitions of magma, monoid, ring, field and integral domain were checked in this text. References of the form I, §4, no. 3 refer to its internal numbering, not PDF page numbers. Most remaining references identify relevant paragraphs rather than claiming a checked proposition-by-proposition correspondence. Statements here are our own formulations of standard mathematics. For French edition information see the [official Bourbaki bibliography](https://www.bourbaki.fr/Ouvrages.html).

AS:BS.title: Theory of Sets
AS:BS.citation:
**[BS] Nicolas Bourbaki, *Theory of Sets*, chapters I–IV**, Springer, 2004 linked edition, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-59309-3). Sets, maps, equivalence relations, quotients, cardinality and the general language of structures are the background supplied by ST.

The main reference for this chapter is [B]. Its groups-with-operators statements are used only in the ordinary-group specialisation. Our elementary examples refer back to the arithmetic results already sourced in [NS](number_systems.md#13-bibliographic-key-and-verification-status). The existence of maximal ideals, when included, is marked with its use of Zorn's lemma; it is not included among the choice-free constructions.

LA:B.title: Algebra I: Chapters 1–3
LA:B.citation: Nicolas Bourbaki, Algebra I: Chapters 1–3, English translation, Hermann/Addison-Wesley, 1974; Springer reprint, 1989. Chapter II: Linear Algebra; chapter III: Tensor Algebras, Exterior Algebras, Symmetric Algebras. References use internal chapter/section numbering. The table of contents was consulted; individual proposition locators have not all been checked.

LA:AX.title: Linear Algebra Done Right
LA:AX.citation: Fourth edition, Springer, 2024; author-hosted corrected PDF dated 16 August 2026. Section references refer to this edition. Used particularly for finite-dimensional inner-product and spectral theory. Statements here are independently formulated. Axler usually takes the scalar field to be ℝ or ℂ. Entries stated over an arbitrary field record standard extensions of the elementary arguments, not a claim that the book uses that full generality.

LA:DM.title: Notes for MA221 Lecture 18: Symmetric eigenvalue problems and the SVD
LA:DM.citation: University of California, Berkeley, 29 October 2009. Rayleigh quotient and Courant–Fischer sections. The displayed min–min on the second side of the first minimax formula is a typographical error; the proof uses min–max. Our formulas use increasing eigenvalue order.

NS:BS.title: Theory of Sets
NS:BS.citation: **[BS] Nicolas Bourbaki, *Theory of Sets*, chapters I–IV**, Springer, 2004 linked edition, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-59309-3). Chapter II supplies sets, products, relations and mappings; chapter III supplies order, cardinals and integers. See also the [official bibliography](https://www.bourbaki.fr/Ouvrages.html) for the French editions. We use this as the main background reference for order and the set-theoretic construction of natural numbers.

NS:BT.title: General Topology, Chapters 1–4
NS:BT.citation: **[BT] Nicolas Bourbaki, *General Topology, Chapters 1–4***, Springer, 1995 linked edition, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-61701-0), chapter IV, “Real Numbers”, pp. 329–418. This is our Bourbaki reference for the real-number system and its order properties. Its development belongs to a broader topological framework; our chosen construction uses Dedekind cuts to keep that framework outside this chapter.
NS:BT.local_availability: Front matter and table of contents only; no full text.

NS:L.title: Foundations of Analysis: The Arithmetic of Whole, Rational, Irrational, and Complex Numbers
NS:L.citation: **[L] Edmund Landau, *Foundations of Analysis: The Arithmetic of Whole, Rational, Irrational, and Complex Numbers***, translated by F. Steinhardt, Chelsea, 1951. Reading guide: I, natural numbers; II, fractions; III, cuts; IV, real numbers; V, complex numbers. Landau is particularly close to this chapter's scope; he is also identified as a precursor in the [Aitken–Holt source guide](https://public.csusm.edu/aitken_html/m378/). His construction and starting convention differ from ours: we include zero in the naturals and construct signed integers before rational numbers. These chapter references are reading recommendations, without checked proposition numbers.

NS:AH.title: Number systems: an axiomatic foundation for algebra, number theory, and analysis
NS:AH.citation: **[AH] Wayne Aitken and Linda Holt, *Number systems: an axiomatic foundation for algebra, number theory, and analysis***, Summer 2019, [author-hosted notes and chapter index](https://public.csusm.edu/aitken_html/m378/). Relevant chapters: 1, Peano axioms; 2, order in $\mathbb{N}$; 4, construction of $\mathbb{Z}$; 5, exploring $\mathbb{Z}$; 7, $\mathbb{Q}$; 9, completeness; 11, $\mathbb{R}$; 12, $\mathbb{C}$. Their chapter 10 uses Cauchy sequences, so it is not our reference for the cut construction. The extra general algebra and analysis in these notes is outside our present scope.

NS:DD.title: Essays on the Theory of Numbers
NS:DD.citation: **[DD] Richard Dedekind, *Essays on the Theory of Numbers***, translated by W. W. Beman, Open Court, 1901, [public-domain edition](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/21016). The essay *Continuity and Irrational Numbers*, especially §§IV–VI, is the historical primary reference for cuts, completeness and arithmetic of real numbers. *The Nature and Meaning of Numbers* provides the companion historical account of natural numbers and induction. Our one-sided cut convention is a modern reformulation.

ST:B.title: Éléments de mathématique. Théorie des ensembles
ST:B.citation: **[B] Nicolas Bourbaki, *Éléments de mathématique. Théorie des ensembles*, chapters I–IV.** The [Bourbaki bibliography](https://www.bourbaki.fr/Ouvrages.html) lists the French volume and its English translation. For a fixed linked edition we use *Theory of Sets*, Springer, 2004, [DOI: 10.1007/978-3-642-59309-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-59309-3). Chapter I: formal mathematics; II: sets; III: ordered sets, cardinals, integers; IV: structures. This is the main reference for the elementary part of this catalogue.

ST:J.title: Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition, revised and expanded
ST:J.citation: **[J] Thomas Jech, *Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition, revised and expanded*, Springer, 2003.** [DOI: 10.1007/3-540-44761-X](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-44761-X). Reading key: chapter 1, axioms; 2, ordinals; 3, cardinals; 4, real numbers; 5, choice and cardinal arithmetic; 6, regularity; 7, filters and Boolean algebras; 8, stationary sets; 12, models; 13, constructibility; 14–15, forcing and applications. This is the main reference for modern axiomatic set theory and independence.

ST:H.title: Naive Set Theory
ST:H.citation: **[H] Paul R. Halmos, *Naive Set Theory*, Springer, 1974 edition.** [DOI: 10.1007/978-1-4757-1645-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-1645-0). A shorter companion for elementary constructions, finite and countable sets, and cardinal comparison.

ST:F.title: Set theory and logic
ST:F.citation: **[F] Gunter Fuchs, *Set theory and logic*, lecture notes, 1 February 2022.** [Author-hosted PDF](https://www.math.csi.cuny.edu/~fuchs/ForcingInSetTheory/LogicScript.pdf). An accessible supplementary source. Checked locators: §2.2, well-founded relations, including Theorem 2.2.11 on collapse; §2.4, cardinal comparison, including Theorem 2.4.4 on Schröder–Bernstein. These notes use their own conventions for some formulations, so we specify our versions below.

AN:B.title: Functions of a Real Variable: Elementary Theory
AN:B.citation: Springer, 2004, translated by Philip Spain. Chapters I (Derivatives), II (Primitives and Integrals), III (Elementary Functions), V (Local Study of Functions). Publisher contents consulted; individual propositions have not been checked in the full text.
AN:B.local_availability: Publisher record only, not the full book.

AN:R.title: Basic Analysis I: Introduction to Real Analysis, Volume I
AN:R.citation: Author-hosted edition, version 6.3, 15 May 2026. Section references are reading locations.

AN:C.title: Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis
AN:C.citation: Author-hosted PDF, consulted October 2026. Section references are reading locations; no edition-specific page numbers are asserted.

MT:AX.title: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis
MT:AX.citation: Springer, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 282, 2020; author-hosted corrected PDF. Sections 2B–2E and 5A provide the main reading locations. General measurable codomains and arbitrary topological Borel spaces are explicit extensions of the elementary inverse-image arguments.

MT:B.title: Integration I: Chapters 1–6
MT:B.citation: Springer, 2004, translated by Sterling K. Berberian. Context reference: Introduction and chapters III–IV on measures on locally compact spaces and extension. Only the introduction/front matter and publisher record were consulted; this source is not claimed as a checked locator for the abstract sigma-algebra-first development.
MT:B.local_availability: Front matter/introduction and publisher metadata only; not the full book.

MT:F.title: Real Analysis: Modern Techniques and Their Applications
MT:F.citation: Second edition, Wiley, 1999. Chapter 1, §1.3, Theorem 1.9 is the reading reference for completion. The cited book passage was not inspected here; this locator remains a reading reference.

TOP:B.title: General Topology: Chapters 1–4
TOP:B.citation: English translation of 1971, Springer reprint. Linked edition DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-61701-0; softcover ISBN 978-3-540-64241-1 (1998). Chapter I, Topological Structures. The contents were inspected for section and numbered-subsection locations; pages are left null where the actual statement was not inspected.
TOP:B.local_availability: Front matter and table of contents only; no full text.
